My Father, Lord of heaven and earth, I am grateful that you hid all this from wise and educated people and showed it to ordinary people. 26Yes, Father, this is what pleased you.
27 My Father has given me everything, and he is the only one who knows the Son. The only one who truly knows the Father is the Son. But the Son wants to tell others about the Father, so they can know him too.
28 If you are tired from carrying heavy burdens, come to me and I will give you rest. 29 Take the yoke I give you. Put it on your shoulders and learn from me. I am gentle and humble, and you will find rest. 30This yoke is easy to bear, and this burden is light.
translation_text:
1Yezu en ta pa'alɛ a zahereba pia la ba yi' la ba'ahɛ la, a ze'ele bilam kiŋɛ ta pa'ala mɛ gee muula a yelefum la ba tinkãra puan.
Yɔn Ko'sɔɔra tum a bitunehi na
2Nananawa, Yɔn en boi pakadeen la gee wum sɛla ti Kiresta la, ita la, a bo' la a zahereba la nuurɛ, 3yeti, “Fum n bala wan wa'am na la bii tu gura ayima?” 4Ti Yezu lebehe ba yeti, “Kiŋɛ ya ta yele Yɔn ya wum gee nyɛ sɛla, 5 fɔɔhi nini pigehɛ mɛ, ti kɔɔrenɔ kina, ti kunkɔma nyɛ tibegɔ, ti wahi wuna, ti kum ihege, ti naheduma wum faarɛ yelefum la. 6Sum boi la se'em en ka piti luta mam zuo.”
Yezu pɛgɛ Yɔn Ko'sɔɔra
7Ban ye' lɛbera la, ti Yezu pɔhɛ tɔgera Yɔn yele bɔ'ɔra nɛrekuuŋɔ la yeti, “Beni ti yamam yuum kɛ̃ muuen la ha ti ya ta bihɛ? Muɔ ti sabeeo tara vɛgelena bii? 8Gee ya yuum kɛ̃ muuen la ha ti ya ta bihɛ la beni? Nɛra en bagɛ ka mɛŋa la banaahi? Bihɛ ya, sɛba en bagerɛ banaahi zi' la na'am yiya. 9Gee ya yuum tugum yehe ti ya bihɛ la beni? Nɔtɔgeha? Ɛ̃ɛ, en yeti ya me wa, a gani nɔtɔgeha. 10 Nɛre kana en bala ti ba gulehɛ a yele yeti,
‘Bihɛ ya, en tuni la n bituneŋa ti ka diŋɛ fum nɛŋa,
Se'em en wan maalɛ fum sore biŋe fum.’
11En yeti ya la yelemɛŋerɛ wa, ti asaala woo ti pɔka dɔgɛ, se'em ka boi ihege na tabelɛ tara zuo gana Yɔn Ko'sɔɔra wa. Gee la bala za'a, se'em en pɔ'ɛ saazuo sɔ'ɔlum puan la gani en. 12 Kɔ'ɔm ze'ele Yɔn Ko'sɔɔra saŋa la wa'am na paaɛ zina, saazuo sɔ'ɔlum la kɔ'ɔm bɔna la gbiregeri puan. Ti sɛba en pɛregɛ la en nyaŋɛ bɔ. 13Se'ere en sɔi la, Nɔtɔgeheba la nɔze'elego la za'a purɛ la bala ti Yɔn ta wa'am na. 14 Ya han wan sakɛ, eŋa en bala en de Eliya ti ba yuum purɛ ti a wan lebe na la. 15Se'em woo en tari tuba, a kɛleha!
16“Gee beni ti en wan dikɛ yamam zina beere nɛreba wa makɛ? Ya ani woo kɔma en zi' da'a yi'ira taaba yeti,
17‘Tumam peebe la yia bahɛ ya, gee ya ka wa;
ti tu kaahɛ, gee ya ka kele kuunɔ.’
18Se'ere en sɔi la, Yɔn yuum wa'am na ka dita ka nyuura ti ba yeti ‘Kulekpa'bɛ'a en dole en.’ 19Ti Asaala Dayua wa'am na dita gee nyuura, ti ba yeti, ‘Bihɛ ya, a dela puya'an daana la danyuura. A dela kubetɔ'ɔhereba la be'emduma zɔ.’ Gee la bala za'a, Yɛm daana tuuma en bo'ori en buurɔ.”
Yele boi tihi zuto
(Luki 10.13-15)
20Ti Yezu pɔhɛ zɛregera tinse'ehi ti a paŋa tuuma tum si puan zo'e, beni zuo ti nɛreba la zagehɛ teere la. 21 “Yele boi yamam Korazinduma zuo! Yele boi yamam Bɛtesaadaduma zuo! Se'ere en sɔi la, paŋa tuuma ana taaba wa han tum ni la Taai la Sidɔn tihi puan, ŋwana ma'a ba tee ni tole tole, gee yɛ susageŋɔ futo, vaaɛ tampɛgɛlum yeele ba mɛhi, pa'ali ti ba tee ya. 22Gee en yeti ya mɛ wa ti, gakerɛ daarɛ, la wan ana ma'ma' bo' Taai la Sidɔn tihi gana yamam. 23 Yamam Kapɛnumduma wa,
Yamam ti'ihɛ ti ya wan kɔ'ɔm zɛkɛ ya mɛhi mɛ zom saazuo?
Aayi, ba wan tari ya na bahɛ la ki'intiŋa.
Se'ere en sɔi la, paŋa tuunsɛ'a en tum bo' ya la han tum ni la Sodom tiŋa puan, ka wan boni na paaɛ zina. 24 Gee en yeti ya mɛ wa, ti gakerɛ daarɛ, la wan ta ana ma'ma' bo' Sodom tiŋa gana yamam.”
Yezu bo' a Sɔ fara fara
(Luki 10.21, 22)
25Sankana puan, ti Yezu tɔgɛ yeti, “Mam bo' n Sɔ saazuo la tiŋa za'a Daana, fara fara se'ere zuo, fum dikɛ yele ana sugɛ yɛm la mi'ilum duma mɛ, gee tugum lilege a bo' kɔmbilɛɛhi. 26Ɛ̃ɛ n Sɔ, fum zu'uhegɔ suboolum en pun daa dɛna se'em n bala. 27 Mam Sɔ dikɛ sɛla woo iŋɛ la mam nu'uhen. Nɛra ka mi' dayua la, han dagena Sɔ la. Nɛra me ka mi' Sɔ la, han dagena dayua la, la se'em ti dayua la bɔta ti a lilege Sɔ la pa'alɛ en.
28“Wa'am ya en zi'an na, yamam sɛba woo n taregɛ gee zɛ zeero, n wan bo' ya vo'ohego. 29 Dikɛ ya mam yɔka la yɔgɛ ya mɛhi, gee zamehɛ mam zi'an, Se'ere en sɔi la, mam dela nɛre ma'ma', gee sigehe n mɛŋa n suure puan. Ya wan nyɛ vo'ohego bo' ya sɛɛhi. 30Se'ere en sɔi la, Mam yɔka la dela naana, ti n zeero la fakɛ.”

english_text:
A Question about the Sabbath
(Mark 2.23-28; Luke 6.1-5)
1 One Sabbath, Jesus and his disciples were walking through some wheat fields. His disciples were hungry and began picking and eating grains of wheat. 2Some Pharisees noticed this and said to Jesus, “Why are your disciples picking grain on the Sabbath? They are not supposed to do this!”
3 Jesus answered:
You surely must have read what David did when he and his followers were hungry. 4 He went into the house of God, and then they ate the sacred loaves of bread that only priests are supposed to eat. 5 Haven't you read in the Law of Moses that the priests are allowed to work in the temple on the Sabbath? But no one says they are guilty of breaking the law of the Sabbath. 6I tell you there is something here greater than the temple. 7 Don't you know what the Scriptures mean when they say, “Instead of offering sacrifices to me, I want you to be merciful to others?” If you knew what this means, you would not condemn these innocent disciples of mine. 8So the Son of Man is Lord over the Sabbath.
A Man with a Paralyzed Hand
(Mark 3.1-6; Luke 6.6-11)
9Jesus left and went into one of their synagogues, 10where there was a man whose hand was paralyzed. Some Pharisees wanted to accuse Jesus of doing something wrong, so they asked him, “Is it right to heal someone on the Sabbath?”
11 Jesus answered, “If one of your sheep fell into a ditch on the Sabbath, wouldn't you lift it out? 12People are worth much more than sheep, and so it is right to do good on the Sabbath.” 13Then Jesus told the man, “Hold out your hand.” The man did, and it became as healthy as the other one.
14The Pharisees left and started making plans to kill Jesus.
God's Chosen Servant
15When Jesus found out what was happening, he left there and large crowds followed him. He healed all of their sick, 16but warned them not to tell anyone about him. 17So God's promise came true, just as Isaiah the prophet had said,
18 “Here is my chosen servant!
I love him,
and he pleases me.
I will give him my Spirit,
and he will bring justice
to the nations.
19He won't shout or yell
or call out in the streets.
20He won't break off a bent reed
or put out a dying flame,
but he will make sure
that justice is done.
21All nations will place
their hope in him.”
Jesus and the Ruler of the Demons
(Mark 3.20-30; Luke 11.14-23; 12.10)
22Some people brought to Jesus a man who was blind and could not talk because he had a demon in him. Jesus healed the man, and then he was able to talk and see. 23The crowds were so amazed they asked, “Could Jesus be the Son of David?”
24 When the Pharisees heard this, they said, “He forces out demons by the power of Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons!”
25Jesus knew what they were thinking, so he said to them:
Any kingdom where people fight each other will end up ruined. And a town or family that fights will soon destroy itself. 26So if Satan fights against himself, how can his kingdom last? 27If I use the power of Beelzebul to force out demons, whose power do your own followers use to force them out? Your followers are the ones who will judge you. 28But when I force out demons by the power of God's Spirit, it proves that God's kingdom has already come to you. 29 How can anyone break into a strong man's house and steal his things, unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he can take everything.
30 If you are not on my side, you are against me. If you don't gather in the harvest with me, you scatter it. 31-32 I tell you any sinful thing you do or say can be forgiven. Even if you speak against the Son of Man, you can be forgiven. But if you speak against the Holy Spirit, you can never be forgiven, either in this life or in the life to come.
A Tree and Its Fruit
(Luke 6.43-45)
33 A good tree produces good fruit, and a bad tree produces bad fruit. You can tell what a tree is like by the fruit it produces. 34 You are a bunch of evil snakes, so how can you say anything good? Your words show what is in your hearts. 35Good people bring good things out of their hearts, but evil people bring evil things out of their hearts. 36I promise you on the day of judgment, everyone will have to account for every careless word they have spoken. 37On that day they will be told they are either innocent or guilty because of the things they have said.
A Sign from Heaven
(Mark 8.11,12; Luke 11.29-32)
38 Some Pharisees and teachers of the Law of Moses said, “Teacher, we want you to show us a sign from heaven.”
39 But Jesus replied:
You want a sign because you are evil and won't believe! But the only sign you will get is the sign of the prophet Jonah. 40 He was in the stomach of a big fish for three days and nights, just as the Son of Man will be deep in the earth for three days and nights. 41 On the day of judgment the people of Nineveh will stand there with you and condemn you. They turned to God when Jonah preached, and yet here is something far greater than Jonah. 42 The Queen of the South will also stand there with you and condemn you. She traveled a long way to hear Solomon's wisdom, and yet here is something much greater than Solomon.
Return of an Evil Spirit
(Luke 11.24-26)
43When an evil spirit leaves a person, it travels through the desert, looking for a place to rest. But when the demon doesn't find a place, 44it says, “I will go back to the home I left.” When it gets there and finds the place empty, clean, and neat, 45it goes off and finds seven other evil spirits even worse than itself. They all come and make their home there, and the person ends up in worse shape than before. That's how it will be with you evil people of today.
Jesus' Mother and Brothers
(Mark 3.31-35; Luke 8.19-21)
46While Jesus was still speaking to the crowds, his mother and brothers came and stood outside because they wanted to talk with him. 47Someone told Jesus, “Your mother and brothers are standing outside and want to talk with you.”
48Jesus answered, “Who is my mother and who are my brothers?” 49Then he pointed to his disciples and said, “These are my mother and my brothers! 50Anyone who obeys my Father in heaven is my brother or sister or mother.”
translation_text:
Vo'ohego Dabeherɛ dia aaheŋɔ
(Maki 2.23-28; Luki 6.1-5)
1 Saŋa kaŋa la, ti Yezu la a zahereba la dɔla va'am puan tɔla vo'ohego dabeherɛ, ti a zahereba la kom duna, ti ba kɔ'ɔra va'am la puan ki ɔbera. 2Farasiiduma la en nyɛ ŋwana la, ba yele en yeti, “Bihɛ, fum zahereba la iti la sɛla en dagi ba iŋɛ vo'ohego dabeherɛ puan.” 3 Ti Yezu yele ba yeti, “Yamam ka kãalɛ Deviti la a nɛreba en yuum iŋɛ se'em, ba kom en yuum duni la? 4 Deviti yuum kɛ̃ la pu'uhegɔ yire la puan ta obe tuulum boroboro la n de kihere bo' eŋa bii a nɛreba la ti ba obe, han dagena malema daana la ma'a. 5 Bii ya ka kãalɛ nɔze'elego la puan, ti vo'ohego dabehere la, malema duma la en boi pu'uhegɔ yire la galum vo'ohego dabeherɛ la mɛ gee ti la ka galum? 6N yeti ya mɛ wa, ti sɛla en gani pu'uhegɔ yire la boi ka'lam. 7 Gee ya han mi' ni yetɔgebuna wa vuurɛ. ‘Mam eere la nimbɔ'zɔrɛ gee dagena kaabegɔ,’ ya kan gakɛ ni sɛba en ka galum la. 8Se'ere en sɔi la, Asaala dayua la n de vo'ohego dabeherɛ la Daana.”
Buraa nu'o en ki
(Maki 3.1-6; Luki 6.6-11)
9Ti Yezu bahɛ bilam gee kɛ̃ ba zamehegɔ yire la puan. 10Bihɛ, ti buraa bɔna bini ti ka nu'o ki. Ti ba soke Yezu yeti, “La de ma'a, ti ba tibera vo'ohego dabeherɛ yo'?” Ba soke ŋwana la ba ta'am zɛregɛ en. 11 Ti a yele ba yeti, “Han deni yamam ayima en tari ni pehego kuyina ti ku lu bulega puan vo'ohego dabeherɛ la, ya kan yaaɛ ni kɔ? 12Asaala ka gani pehego? Bala zuo, la de ma'a ti nɛra tum sum vo'ohego dabeherɛ la.” 13Gee nyaa yele buraa la yeti, “Tiɛ fum nu'o la.” Ti buraa la tiɛ ka nu'o la, ti ku iŋɛ sum, kɔ'ɔm ana wuu nu'o kuna la. 14Gee Farasiiduma la yehe mɛ ta ku nuurɛ la taaba ti ba bihɛ ban wan iŋɛ se'em ku en.
Yinɛ tuntuna ti a looe
15Yezu en ta baŋɛ dina wa la, a bahɛ bilam mɛ, ti nɛrekuuŋɔ doohe a poore, ti a tibɛ ba za'a, 16gee ka'am ba la ninmu'urɛ ti, ba da bahɛ ti nɛreba baŋɛ en. 17Dina wa dela, nɔtɔgeha Azaaya en yuum purɛ se'em la wa'am yelemɛŋerɛ na.
18“Bihɛ, mam yameŋa en ŋwana, se'em ti mam looe,
Se'em ti mam suure nɔŋɛ, se'em en tigeri mam nini.
N wan dikɛ n Sia iŋɛ a puan;
a wan muulɛ buurɔ bo' sɛba en dagi Yuda buuri la za'a.
19A kan zabera bii a tahera,
bii nɛra wum a yele sadɔtɔ zuo.
20Muɔ seko en kɔ'ɛ nyure, a kan kikɛ kɔ bahɛ.
Bii a pebele bugum n diti bahɛ.
Gura ti yelemɛŋerɛ ta sooe.
21A yu'urɛ puan ti sɛba en dagi Yuuduma me wan tara beere puti'irɛ.”
Yezu la Beelezebule
(Maki 3.20-30; Luki 11.14-23)
22Ti ba tari buraa ti kulekpa'bɛ'a dɔla ka, ti ka dɛna fua la gɔɔŋɔ wa'am Yezu zi'an na ti a tibɛ ka, ti buraa wa en de gɔŋɔ wa tana tɔgera gee nyɛta. 23Ti la iŋɛ nɛrekuuŋɔ la za'a pakerɛ zo'e zo'e, ti ba yɛta yeti, “Nɛra wa wan ta'am dɛna Deviti dayua?” 24Gee Farasiiduma la en wum dina wa la, ba yeti, “Beelezebule en de kulekpa'bɛ'ɛhi naba la en dole buraa wa ti ka tana sa'aha kulekpa'bɛ'ɛhi la.” 25Yezu n baŋɛ ban ti'ihɛ se'em la, ti a yele ba yeti, “Sɔ'ɔlum sebo en welege zabera la bu mɛŋa wan lebege daboo. Tiŋa bii Yire me ka boi welege zabera la de mɛŋa gee wan ta'am ze'ele. 26Bala, Sagena la han tulege sa'aha Sagena, a welege mɛ zabera la a mɛŋa. A sɔ'ɔlum la yeti bu iŋɛ la ŋwani ze'ele? 27Bala, mam han tara Beelezebule sa'aha kulekpa'bɛ'ɛhi, gee yamam nɛreba la me tari la ani sa'aha kulekpa'bɛ'ɛhi? Bala zuo, ya mɛhi zahereba la en wan gakɛ ya. 28Gee la han dɛna la Yinɛ Sia la ti mam tara sa'aha kulekpa'bɛ'ɛhi, Yinɛ sɔ'ɔlum la yi paaɛ ya mɛ me na n bala. 29Bii nɛra wan iŋɛ la ŋwani ta'am kɔ' kɛ̃ paŋa daana yire fã a lɔgerɔ, gee ka lu' paŋa daana la biŋe yia? Bala ti a nyaa wan ta'am fã yire la suŋa suŋa. 30Se'em en ka suni la mam zaberɛ mɛ la mam, Se'em me en ka ka'aheri bɔ'ɔra mam, yiregerɛ bahera mɛ. 31Bala zuo, mam yeti, nɛreba wan nyɛ sugeri dia be'em la zɛɛhi woo puan, gee se'em woo en zeem Fa'a Sia la kan nyɛ sugeri dia. 32 Se'em woo en tɔgɛ se'ere pɔ'ɛ Asaala Dayua wa, wan nyɛ sugeri dia, gee se'em woo en tɔgɛ se'ere pɔ'ɛ Fa'a Sia la kan malum nyɛ sugeri dia, zina bii beere.
Tia la ka wala
(Luki 6.43-45)
33 “Bihɛ tia suŋa gee ka wala me wan ani suŋa. Bii da bihɛ tia suŋa gee ka wala me ka ana suŋa. Se'ere en sɔi la, tia wala en pa'alɛ kan de tisɛka. 34 Yamam kampɛbibehi wa, yamam yeti ya iŋɛ la ŋwani tɔgera yelesuma, gee dɛna be'em duma wa? Se'ere en sɔi la, sɛla en boi suuren zo'e zo'e la ti nuurɛ tɔgera. 35Nɛresuma yeheri la yelesuma sɛ'a en boi a lɔgesunɔ la puan, ti nɛrebɛ'a me, yeheri yeletoseto en boi a lɔge tooro la puan la. 36Mam yeti ya ti, gakerɛ daarɛ, nɛrawoo wan yele yetɔgeyooro seto ti ba tɔgɛ la ba nɔya. 37“Fum tugum en wan ta bo' fum buurɔ, fum tugum en wan ta sagum hɔ.”
Yona daalehum
(Maki 8.11, 12; Luki 11.29-32)
38 Ti gɔnmi'ineba la Farasiiduma yele en yeti, “Pa'ala, tu boti tu nyɛ la daalehum fum zi'an.” 39Gee Yezu lebehe ba yeti, “Be'em la baga kaabegɔ buuri saŋa en eere daalehum, gee daalehum ka boi wan bo' ba, han dagena nɔtɔgeha Yona daalehum la. 40 Wuu Yona en yuum boi ko'om bunsɛla la puuren dabeha atã wuntɛɛŋa la yu'uŋɔ se'em la, bala mɛa ti Asaala dayua wa wan ta bɔna tiŋa wa puan ha dabeha atã, wuntɛɛŋa la yu'uŋɔ. 41 Ninevɛ tiŋa nɛreba gakerɛ daarɛ la, wan ta ihege la zina beere nɛreba wa, tɔgɛ lubɛ ba. Se'ere en sɔi la, se'ere en sɔi la, ban yuum wum Yona muulegɔ la, ba kɔ'ɔm tee ba vom mɛ. Nyaa bihɛ ya, se'em en gani Yona n ŋwana. 42 Tiŋanuurɛ pɔgenaba la, gakerɛ daarɛ wan ta ihege la zina beere nɛreba wa tɔgɛ lubɛ ba. Se'ere en sɔi la, a yuum ze'ele la zi'an en zaaɛ wa'am na ti a kelehe Solomɔn yɛm la. Nyaa Bihɛ ya, se'em en gani Solomɔn n ŋwana.
Sɛfi'iha lɛbega na
(Luki 11.24-26)
43“Sɛfi'iha han ni yehe nɛra puan, ka ni ɛɛra tuuna la kpaahenɛ puan, ɛɛra vo'ohego zi'an, gee ka nyɛ. 44A ni yeti, ‘N wan lebe la en yikɛka la ti n ze'ele de puan na la.’ A han paaɛ na, a nyɛ ti yire la ze' la voore, piihɛ, ti sɛla woo ana suŋa. 45A nyaa ni lebe mɛ ta tari Sɛfi'iha siyopɔi se'ehi tuuma n fi'ɛ gana eŋa, ti ba wa'am na kɛ̃. Ti nɛra kaŋa ba'ahegɔ nyaa ni ba' sagum mɛ gana a yia la. Bala mɛa ti la wan ana bo' zina beere be'em nɛreba wa.”
Yezu yireduma
(Maki 3.31-35; Luki 8.19-21)
46Yezu en kelum bɔna bini tɔgera bɔ'ɔra nɛrekuuŋɔ la, bihɛ, a ma la a suurɔ wa'am na zɛ'a yiŋa ti ba tɔgɛ la en. 47Ti Nɛra ayima yele en yeti, “Bihɛ, fum ma la fum suurɔ ze' yiŋa bɔta ti ba tɔgɛ bo' fum.” 48Gee se'em en yele en ŋwana wa la, Yezu lebe en yeti, “Mam ma dela ani, ti en suurɔ dɛna bani?” 49Gee tiɛ nu'o pa'ala a zahereba la, gee yeti, “Bihɛ, Mam ma la mam suurɔ n ŋwana. 50Se'ere en sɔi la, se'em woo en tuni mam sɔ n boi saazuo ha sumboolum, nɛre eŋa en de mam suuɔ, mam taya, la mam ma.”

english_text:
A Story about a Farmer
(Mark 4.1-9; Luke 8.4-8)
1That same day Jesus left the house and went out beside Lake Galilee, where he sat down to teach. 2 Such large crowds gathered around him that he had to sit in a boat, while the people stood on the shore. 3Then he taught them many things by using stories. He said:
A farmer went out to scatter seed in a field. 4While the farmer was scattering the seed, some of it fell along the road and was eaten by birds. 5Other seeds fell on thin, rocky ground and quickly started growing because the soil wasn't very deep. 6But when the sun came up, the plants were scorched and dried up, because they did not have deep roots. 7Some other seeds fell where thornbushes grew up and choked the plants. 8But a few seeds did fall on good ground where the plants produced 100 or 60 or 30 times as much as was scattered. 9If you have ears, pay attention!
Why Jesus Used Stories
(Mark 4.10-12; Luke 8.9,10)
10Jesus' disciples came to him and asked, “Why do you use stories to speak to the people?”
11Jesus answered:
I have explained the secrets about the kingdom of heaven to you, but not to others. 12 Everyone who has something will be given more. But people who don't have anything will lose even what little they have. 13I use stories when I speak to them because when they look, they cannot see, and when they listen, they cannot hear or understand. 14 So God's promise came true, just as the prophet Isaiah had said,
“These people will listen
and listen,
but never understand.
They will look and look,
but never see.
15All of them have
stubborn minds!
They refuse to listen;
they cover their eyes.
They cannot see or hear
or understand.
If they could,
they would turn to me,
and I would heal them.”
16 But God has blessed you, because your eyes can see and your ears can hear! 17Many prophets and good people were eager to see what you see and to hear what you hear. But I tell you they did not see or hear.
Jesus Explains the Story about the Farmer
(Mark 4.13-20; Luke 8.11-15)
18Now listen to the meaning of the story about the farmer:
19The seeds that fell along the road are the people who hear the message about the kingdom, but don't understand it. Then the evil one comes and snatches the message from their hearts. 20The seeds that fell on rocky ground are the people who gladly hear the message and accept it at once. 21But they don't have deep roots, and they don't last very long. As soon as life gets hard or the message gets them in trouble, they give up.
22The seeds that fell among the thornbushes are also people who hear the message. But they start worrying about the needs of this life and are fooled by the desire to get rich. So the message gets choked out, and they never produce anything. 23The seeds that fell on good ground are the people who hear and understand the message. They produce as much as 100 or 60 or 30 times what was planted.
Weeds among the Wheat
24Jesus then told them this story:
The kingdom of heaven is like what happened when a farmer scattered good seed in a field. 25But while everyone was sleeping, an enemy came and scattered weed seeds in the field and then left.
26When the plants came up and began to mature, the farmer's servants could see the weeds. 27The servants came and asked, “Sir, didn't you scatter good seed in your field? Where did these weeds come from?”
28“An enemy did this,” he replied.
His servants then asked, “Do you want us to go out and pull up the weeds?”
29“No!” he answered. “You might also pull up the wheat. 30Leave the weeds alone until harvest time. Then I'll tell my workers to gather the weeds and tie them up and burn them. But I'll order them to store the wheat in my barn.”
Stories about a Mustard Seed and Yeast
(Mark 4.30-32; Luke 13.18-21)
31Jesus told them another story:
The kingdom of heaven is like what happens when a farmer plants a mustard seed in a field. 32Although it is the smallest of all seeds, it grows larger than any garden plant and becomes a tree. Birds even come and nest on its branches.
33Jesus also said:
The kingdom of heaven is like what happens when a woman mixes a little yeast into three big batches of flour. Finally, all the dough rises.
The Reason for Teaching with Stories
(Mark 4.33,34)
34Jesus used stories when he spoke to the people. In fact, he did not tell them anything without using stories. 35 So God's promise came true, just as the prophet had said,
“I will use stories
to speak my message
and to explain things hidden
since the creation
of the world.”
Jesus Explains the Story about the Weeds
36After Jesus left the crowd and went inside, his disciples came to him and said, “Explain to us the story about the weeds in the wheat field.”
37Jesus answered:
The one who scattered the good seed is the Son of Man. 38The field is the world, and the good seeds are the people who belong to the kingdom. The weeds are those who belong to the evil one, 39and the one who scattered them is the devil. The harvest is the end of time, and angels are the ones who bring in the harvest.
40Weeds are gathered and burned. That's how it will be at the end of time. 41The Son of Man will send out his angels, and they will gather from his kingdom everyone who does wrong or causes others to sin. 42Then he will throw them into a flaming furnace, where people will cry and grit their teeth in pain. 43 But everyone who has done right will shine like the sun in their Father's kingdom. If you have ears, pay attention!
A Hidden Treasure
44The kingdom of heaven is like what happens when someone finds a treasure hidden in a field and buries it again. Such a person is happy and goes and sells everything in order to buy that field.
A Valuable Pearl
45The kingdom of heaven is like what happens when a shop owner is looking for fine pearls. 46After finding a very valuable one, the owner goes and sells everything in order to buy that pearl.
A Fish Net
47The kingdom of heaven is like what happens when a net is thrown into a lake and catches all kinds of fish. 48When the net is full, it is dragged to the shore, and the fishermen sit down to separate the fish. They keep the good ones, but throw the bad ones away. 49That's how it will be at the end of time. Angels will come and separate the evil people from the ones who have done right. 50Then those evil people will be thrown into a flaming furnace, where they will cry and grit their teeth in pain.
New and Old Treasures
51Jesus asked his disciples if they understood all these things. They said, “Yes, we do.”
52So he told them, “Every student of the Scriptures who becomes a disciple in the kingdom of heaven is like someone who brings out new and old treasures from the storeroom.”
The People of Nazareth Turn against Jesus
(Mark 6.1-6; Luke 4.16-30)
53When Jesus had finished telling these stories, he left 54and went to his hometown. He taught in their synagogue, and the people were so amazed that they asked, “Where does he get all this wisdom and the power to work these miracles? 55Isn't he the son of the carpenter? Isn't Mary his mother, and aren't James, Joseph, Simon, and Judas his brothers? 56Don't his sisters still live here in our town? How can he do all this?” 57 So the people were upset because of what he was doing.
But Jesus said, “Prophets are honored by everyone, except the people of their hometown and their own family.” 58And because the people did not have any faith, Jesus did not work many miracles there.
translation_text:
Yinɛ sɔ'ɔlum makerɛ
(Maki 4.1-9; Luki 8.4-8)
1De daarɛ mɛa ti Yezu yehe yire ta zi'a ateko nuuren. 2 Ti nɛrekuuŋɔ en ka tã ita lagehɛ a zi'an na, ti a zom uureŋɔ zuo zi'a bini gee ti nɛrekuuŋɔ la zɛ'a ko'om la nuuren. 3Ti a yele ba yɛla zo'e zo'e mageha puan yeti, “Kelehe ya! Buta en yehe ti a burɛ. 4Ti en buti la, ti bumbuura la basɛba zɔgɛ sore zuo, ti niihe wa'am na di ba. 5Ti basɛba lu tahi zi'an, zi'an ti tintɔnɔ ka zo'e, Ti ba yehe kalam, tintɔnɔ en ka zo'e la zuo. 6Gee wuntɛɛŋa en ŋmɛ na la, ba zɛkɛ mɛ, ba nyɛga en ka sige la zuo, ba ki mɛ. 7Ti Bumbuura la basɛba zɔgɛ gu'uhi puan, ti gu'uhi la zo'e na kpãrɛ ba. 8Ti Bumbuura la basɛba me zɔgɛ pu'uhegɔ zi'an yagum zuto, basɛba yagum zuto kɔbega kɔbega, ti basɛba yagum zuto piyoobe piyoobe, ti basɛba me yagum zuto pihitã pihitã. 9Bahɛ ya ti se'em woo en tari tuba ti a wuna, a kɛleha.”
10Pooren ti a zahereba la wa'am a zi'an na soke en yeti, “Ŋwani ti fum tara mageha tɔgera bɔ'ɔra nɛreba?” 11Ti a lerege ba yeti, “Han dɛna yamam, ba bo' yamam mɛ ti ya bɔkera saazuo sɔ'ɔlum la yele sɛ'a en sugɛ, gee ba ka bo' bamam bala. 12 Se'ere en sɔi la, se'em en tari la, ba wan bo' en pa'ahɛ ti en malum tara gaŋɛ. Gee se'em me en ka tari sɛla la, La fii wa ti ba tara la, ba wan to'e la a zi'an. 13Se'ere zuo ti mam tara mageha tɔgera bɔ'ɔra ba la dela, ‘Ba biheri, gee ba ka nyɛti, ba kɛlehi, gee ba wuni, bii ba bɔkera.’ 14 Bana puan ti Azaaya yelefum la wa'am asira na.
‘Ya sirum wan kɛleha gee ya kan malum bɔkɛ,
ya me sirum wan biha gee ya kan malum nyɛ.
15Se'ere en sɔi la, nɛrebana wa puti'ira ba' ki mɛ,
ti ba tuba kpa' ka wuna,
ti ba kɔ'ɔm mum ba nini,
ti ba da bihɛ la ba nini la,
gee kɛleha la ba tuba la,
gee bɔkera la ba suya, la ba ŋmɛregɛ lebena,
ti en tibɛ ba.’
16 Gee sum boi yamam nini puan. Se'ere en sɔi la, i nyɛti, ti sum bɔna ya tuba puan, se'ere en sɔi la, a wuni. 17Yelemɛŋerɛ ti en yɛta ya wa, nɔtɔgeheba, la nɛretuntɔɔ duma zo'e zo'e yuum boti ba nyɛ yamam en nyɛ sɛla wa mɛ, gee ka nyɛ la, gee bɔta ti ba wum yamam en wum sɛla wa, gee ka wum.
18“Wum ya buta la makerɛ vuurɛ. 19Se'em woo en ni wum sɔ'ɔlum la yɛla gee ka bɔkɛ a, Sagena la ni wa'am mɛ na zɛ sɛla ti ba burɛ a suuren la. Bana en de bumbuura sɛ'a en zɔgɛ sore zuo la. 20Han dɛna sɛba en zɔgɛ tahi zi'an la, dela se'em en ni wum yelefum la, to'e bu bilam bilam la nyɛɛma, 21gee nɛre-ina daana wa nyɛga ka ba, gee a yeen ŋmibe la fii wa, gee daaŋɔ bii mɛlehegɔ han paaɛ en yelefum wa zuo, a duma ni lu mɛ bilam bilam. 22Han dɛna sɛba en zɔgɛ gu'uhi puan la, eŋa dela se'em en wum yelefum la, gee ti tiŋa wa zuo yɛla nyɛlum la tarega pa'ahɛ la ni gu' yelefum la ti bu ka ta'am wam sɛla. 23Gee bumbuura sɛ'a ti ba burɛ pu'uhegɔ zi'an la, bamam en de sɛba en wum yelefum la gee bɔkɛ bɔ, bana en de sɛba en wam biili zo'e zo'e, ti sɛba yagum kɔbega kɔbega, ti sɛba me yagum piyoobe piyoobe, ti basɛba me yagum pihitã pihitã.”
24Yezu le dikɛ la makerɛ deyima biŋe ba yeti, “Saazuo sɔ'ɔlum la wan dikɛ makɛ mɛ la nɛra en burɛ a bumbuura suma a va'am puan. 25Gee yu'uŋɔ ti nɛrawoo ta giha la, ti dindaana kiŋɛ ta lobege mɔyileŋo pa'ahɛ ki la puan gee kiŋɛ. 26Bumbuura la en ta zo'e ita nini la, ti mɔyileŋo la me ihege na, lagum zɛ'a la ba. 27Ti yidaana la yamehi wa'am na yele en yeti, ‘Daana, fum ka burɛ la bumbuura suma va'am la puan? Gee mɔyileŋo la ze'ele la bɛ na?’ 28Ti a lerege ba yeti, ‘Dima en tum de bala.’ Ti yamehi la yele en yeti, ‘Fum boti tu kiŋɛ ta vɔ mɔyileŋo la bahɛ?’ 29Ti a lerege ba yeti, ‘Aayi,’ ya han ta vuura mɔyileŋo la, ki la wan lagum doohe. 30Bahɛ ya ti ba za'a lagum zɔ'ɔra gura buŋa saŋa. Buŋa saŋa la, en wan ta yele buneba la yeti, ‘Kɛ̃ ya mɔyileŋo la yia bobe ba bobene bobene ba nyɔ', gee nyaa bum dia la iŋɛ en bããren.’ ”
31Ti a le dikɛ makerɛ deyima biŋe ba yeti, “Yinɛ sɔ'ɔlum la ani wuu nangembiileho ti nɛra burɛ a va'am puan, 32Biiliho buna wa pɔ'ɛ mɛ biila wuu puan, gee bu han yehe na, bu ni dɛna la tuntuo kãtɛ, nyaa ta lebege tia, ti niihe nyaa ni wa'am na tɛ' ba tugerɔ ka zuo.”
33Ti Yezu le yele ba makerɛ deyima yeti, “Yinɛ sɔ'ɔlum la ani me wuu dabelɛ fii ti pɔka dikɛ gɛregɛ wama atã zom, ti bu bahɛ ti zom la za'a ihege se'em la.”
34Yezu yele nɛrekuuŋɔ la yele ana za'a la mageha puan, a ka tɔgɛ se'ere bo' ba ka dikɛ doohe mageha puan. 35Dina iŋɛ ti nɔtɔgeha la purega la wa'am asira na. A yuum purɛ yeti,
“Mam wan ya'ɛ en nuurɛ tɔgɛ la mageha,
N wan muulɛ sɛla en sugɛ tiŋa wa pi'ileŋo na.”
36Ti Yezu bahɛ nɛrekuuŋɔ la gee kiŋɛ ta kɛ̃ yise'ere ti a kɛ̃'ɛ̃ra la. Ti a zahereba la paaɛ soke en yeti, “Garehɛ bu tɔ va'am puan mɔyileŋo makerɛ la vuurɛ.” 37Ti a lerege ba yeti, “Se'em en burɛ bumbuulesuma la dela Asaala Dayua la. 38Va'am la dela timpaberɛ wa, ti bumbuulesuma la dɛna sɔ'ɔlum la kɔma, ti mɔyileŋo la dɛna Sagena la kɔma, 39dima la en burɛ mɔyileŋo la dela Sagena la, ti buŋa la me dɛna timpaberɛ wa ba'ahegɔ saŋa, ti buneba la dɛna Yinɛ suŋereba. 40Wuu mɔyileŋo la ti ba lagehɛ nyɔ' se'em la bugum la, la wan ta ana la bala tiŋa wa ba'ahegɔ saŋa. 41Asaala dayua la wan ta tum a suŋereba na, ti ba doohe a sɔ'ɔlum la puan lagehɛ sɛla woo en baheri ti nɛreba tuna be'em, la tuumbe'ero duma la za'a yehe a sɔ'ɔlum la puan, 42nyaa tari ba ta lobe bahɛ bugum peelum la puan. Bilam ti ba wan kaaha gee ɔbera nyɛna. 43Gee tuntɔɔduma la wan ta nyakera mɛ wuu wuntɛɛŋa ba Sɔ sɔ'ɔlum la puan. Bahɛ ti se'em woo en tari tuba ti a wuna, kɛleha.
44“Saazuo sɔ'ɔlum la ani mɛ wuu tuulum lɔkɔ en sugɛ va'am puan, ti nɛra ayima ta nyɛ kɔ malum sugɛ kɔ, gee nyaa nyɛɛna lɛbera, ta paaɛ vaaɛ sɛla woo ti a tara ta koohe ta da' zi'an la.
45“Le yɛ'ɛha, saazuo sɔ'ɔlum la ani wuu lɛɛba en eeri tuulum nunɔm lɔgesunɔ. 46En ta nyɛ tuulum lɔkɔ kuyima en ba' ana suŋa la, a kiŋɛ mɛ ta koohe sɛla woo ti a tara, wa'am na da' kɔ.
47“Le yɛ'ɛha, saazuo sɔ'ɔlum la ani mɛ wuu yuka ti ba dikɛ lobe mɔgerɛ puan nyɔgɛ zim buuri buuri la. 48Yuka la en ta pirɛ la, ba ve'e ka mɛ dooe doone na, nyaa zi'ire gahɛ zim suma la iŋɛ ba pitɔ puan, gee lobe bumbe'ero la bahɛ. 49Lan wan ta ana se'em ba'ahegɔ saŋa la en bala. Yinɛ suŋereba la wan ta wa'am na, yelehe be'emduma la tuntɔɔduma la puan, 50lobe ba bahɛ bugum peelum la puan, zi'an ti ba wan ta kaaha gee ɔbera nyɛna.
Lɔgepaala la lɔgekɛgehi
51“Yamam bɔkɛ yele ana wa za'a?” Ti ba lerege yeti, “Ɛ̃ɛ.” 52Ti a yele ba yeti, “Bala zuo, gɔnmina se'em woo en zamehɛ mina saazuo sɔ'ɔlum wa yɛla ani wuu Yidaana en gbɛ'ɛri lɔgepaala la lɔgekɛgehi a lɔgerɔ puan yɛhera na la.” 53Yezu en ba'ahɛ mageha ana wa la, a bahɛ bilam mɛ.
Ba zagehɛ Yezu Nazareti
(Maki 6.1-6; Luki 4.16-30)
54Ti Yezu wa'am a mɛŋa tiŋa na, pɔhɛ pa'ala nɛreba zamehegɔ yiya la puan ti la iŋɛ nɛreba la pakerɛ zo'e zo'e. Ti ba yɛta yeti, “Burakana nyɛ yɛm buna wa la paŋa tuun-ana wa la bɛ? 55Dagi ena en de kpa'ara la dayua la? Dagi a ma yu'urɛ n yi'iri Mɛɛri la? Dagi a suurɔ en de Yemesi, Yosefe, Simɔn la Yudasi? 56Dagi a suurɔ za'a en naaɛ la tɔ kɛ̃'ɛ̃ra wa? Bɛha, ti buraa kana wa nyɛ yele ana za'a?” 57 Ti ba zeem en, ti Yezu lerege ba yeti, “Nɔtɔgeha tari na'ahegɔ mɛ zi'an woo, han dagena a mɛŋa tiŋa bii a mɛŋa yiya puan ma'a.” 58Ŋwana zuo, Yezu ka tum daalehum tuuma zo'e bilam, ban ka nam bo' en la zuo.

english_text:
The Death of John the Baptist
(Mark 6.14-29; Luke 9.7-9)
1About this time Herod the ruler heard the news about Jesus 2and told his officials, “This is John the Baptist! He has come back from death, and that's why he has the power to work these miracles.”
3-4 Herod had earlier arrested John and had him chained and put in prison. He did this because John had told him, “It isn't right for you to take Herodias, the wife of your brother Philip.” 5Herod wanted to kill John. But the people thought John was a prophet, and Herod was afraid of what they might do.
6When Herod's birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced for the guests. She pleased Herod 7so much he swore to give her whatever she wanted. 8But the girl's mother told her to say, “Here on a serving plate I want the head of John the Baptist!”
9Herod was sorry for what he had said. But he did not want to break the promise he had made in front of his guests. So he ordered a guard 10to go to the prison and cut off John's head. 11It was taken on a serving plate to the girl, and she gave it to her mother. 12John's followers took his body and buried it. Then they told Jesus what had happened.
Jesus Feeds Five Thousand
(Mark 6.30-44; Luke 9.10-17; John 6.1-14)
13After Jesus heard about John, he crossed Lake Galilee to go to some place where he could be alone. But the crowds found out and followed him on foot from the towns. 14When Jesus got out of the boat, he saw the large crowd. He felt sorry for them and healed everyone who was sick.
15That evening the disciples came to Jesus and said, “This place is like a desert, and it's already late. Let the crowds leave, so they can go to the villages and buy some food.”
16Jesus replied, “They don't have to leave. Why don't you give them something to eat?”
17But they said, “We have only five small loaves of bread and two fish.” 18Jesus asked his disciples to bring the food to him, 19and he told the crowd to sit down on the grass. Jesus took the five loaves and the two fish. He looked up toward heaven and blessed the food. Then he broke the bread and handed it to his disciples, and they gave it to the people.
20After everyone had eaten all they wanted, Jesus' disciples picked up twelve large baskets of leftovers.
21There were about 5,000 men who ate, not counting the women and children.
Jesus Walks on the Water
(Mark 6.45-52; John 6.15-21)
22At once, Jesus made his disciples get into a boat and start back across the lake. But he stayed until he had sent the crowds away. 23Then he went up on a mountain where he could be alone and pray. Later in the evening, he was still there.
24By this time the boat was a long way from the shore. It was going against the wind and was being tossed around by the waves. 25A little while before morning, Jesus came walking on the water toward his disciples. 26When they saw him, they thought he was a ghost. They were terrified and started screaming.
27At once, Jesus said to them, “Don't worry! I am Jesus. Don't be afraid.”
28Peter replied, “Lord, if it really is you, tell me to come to you on the water.”
29“Come on!” Jesus said. Peter then got out of the boat and started walking on the water toward him.
30But when Peter saw how strong the wind was, he was afraid and started sinking. “Save me, Lord!” he shouted.
31At once, Jesus reached out his hand. He helped Peter up and said, “You surely don't have much faith. Why do you doubt?”
32When Jesus and Peter got into the boat, the wind died down. 33The men in the boat worshiped Jesus and said, “You really are the Son of God!”
Jesus Heals Sick People in Gennesaret
(Mark 6.53-56)
34Jesus and his disciples crossed the lake and came to shore near the town of Gennesaret. 35The people found out he was there, and they sent word to everyone who lived in this part of the country. So they brought all the sick people to Jesus. 36They begged him just to let them touch his clothes, and everyone who did was healed.
translation_text:
Yɔn Ko'sɔɔra la kum
(Maki 6.14-29; Luki 9.7-9)
1Sankaŋa puan, ti Hɛrɔd en de timbihera la wum Yezu yele mɛ, 2nyaa a yele a tuntuneba yeti, “Ena wa dela Yɔn Ko'sɔɔra la. A ihege mɛ a kum la puan. Ŋwana zuo ti pansina wa tuna a puan la.” 3 Se'ere en sɔi la, Hɛrɔd pugum nyɔkɛ Yɔn mɛ, ba' en, dikɛ en iŋɛ paka deo puan, doohe Hɛrɔdiya en de Hɛrɔd suuɔ Filipi pɔga la zuo. 4 Se'ere en sɔi la, Yɔn yeti Hɛrɔd mɛ saŋa woo ti, “La kihi mɛ ti a fã a suuɔ pɔga di.” 5La Hɛrɔd en daa pun bɔta ti a ku Yɔn la, a daa zoti la nɛrekuuŋɔ la dabeem, se'ere en sɔi la, bamam nam ti Yɔn dela nɔtɔgeha. 6Gee Hɛrɔd dɔgum daarɛ en wa paaɛ, ti Hɛrɔdiya poyua wa' nɛrekuuŋɔ la nɛŋan, ti Hɛrɔd puurɛ pee paaɛ paaɛ, 7ti la paaɛ en, ti a biŋe nuurɛ la pɔtɛ ti a wan bo' en sɛla woo ti a soke en. 8Ti pugela la ma ɛbegɛ en ti a yeti, “Dikɛ Yɔn Ko'sɔɔra la zuo iŋɛ lapɛrega puan bo' ze'ele ka'lam bo' mam.” 9Ti Naba wa suure sagum, gee en diŋɛ biŋe a nuurɛ la, la a saama la en zi' dɛla taaba la zuo, ti a bo' nuurɛ ti ba ta tari ku na. 10Gee nyaa tum ti ba kiŋɛ ta fike Yɔn zuo paka deo la puan na. 11Ti ba tari zuo la, la lapɛrega puan na bo' pugela la, ti ka tari ta bo' ka ma. 12Ti Yɔn zahereba la wa'am na dikɛ a iŋa la ta laaɛ gee kiŋɛ ta yele Yezu.
Tuha anuu diihego
(Maki 6.30-44; Luki 9.10-17; Yɔn 6.1-14)
13Yezu en wum dina la, a bahɛ bilam mɛ gee kiŋɛ ta kɛ̃ uureŋɔ kiŋɛ zi'an ti nɛreba ka bɔna bilam a ma'a. Gee nɛrekuuŋɔ la en wum bala la, ba yehe la ba tihi puan kiŋɛ la nama doohe a poore. 14Yezu en ze'ele uureŋɔ la puan sige na la, a nyɛ nɛrekuuŋɔ la mɛ, zɔ ba nimbu'ɔ, gee tibɛ sɛba en wa'am na la nɛreba sɛba n bɛ̃'ɛri la. 15Yinɛ en ta luta la, ti a zahereba la paaɛ a zi'an yele en yeti, “Ka'lam dela muɔ puan, gee ti yinɛ me luta, bahɛ nɛrekuuŋɔ wa ti ba yiregɛ kiŋɛ timbibehi puan la ba ta'am da' dia bo' ba mɛhi.” 16Gee Yezu yele ba yeti, “La dagi ba kiŋɛ, yamam bo' ba sɛla ti ba di.” 17Ti ba lerege en yeti, “Tu ka tari sɛla ka'lam, han dagena boroboro banuu la zim i yi' ma'a.” 18Ti Yezu yeti, “Tari ya ba na bo' mam ka'lam.” 19Gee bo' nɛrekuuŋɔ la nuurɛ ti ba zi'ire muɔ la zuo, gee nyaa to'e boroboro banuu la zim iyi' la, gorege bihɛ saazuo gee purɛ sum, gee nyaa figehe boroboro la bo' a zahereba la, ti a zahereba la me to'e tɔta nɛrekuuŋɔ la. 20Ti ba za'a di ta tigɛ, gee ti ba doohe lagehɛ sɛla ti ba di gee gee la, ti ba pirɛ pitɔ pia la tuyi'. 21Sɛba en di la wan paaɛ wuu buraahi tuha anuu, ti pɔgehi la kɔma ka pa'ahɛ.
Yezu kini ko'om zuo
(Maki 6.45-52; Yɔn 6.15-21)
22Bilam bilam ti a bahɛ ti a zahereba la zom uureŋɔ tole nɛŋa yakera ko'om la yakenɛ deyima la ha, gee ti a leen keehe nɛrekuuŋɔ la. 23N keehe nɛrekuuŋɔ la ba'ahɛ la, a zom la zoore zuo a ma'a ta pu'uha. Ti yinɛ ta ma'ɛ ti a kelum bɔna bini a ma'a, 24gee bala ma'a ti ko'mi'ihi en tu'uhɛ uureŋɔ la, ti ku nan zaaɛ la doone, se'ere en sɔi la, sabeeo la lobere tu'uha ba mɛ. 25Ze'ele gogo kaareŋa anaahi bulika yu'uŋɔ yu'uŋɔ ti Yezu kina ko'om la tu'uha a zahereba la . 26Gee a zahereba la en nyɛ en ti a kini ko'om la zuo la, dabeem en kɛ̃' ba paaɛ paaɛ, ti ba yeti, “A dela kukɔ!” Gee kaahɛ la dabeem. 27Gee bilam bilam ti Yezu tɔgɛ bo' ba yeti, “Da bahɛ ya ti ya paleŋa ɛgera, la dela mam, da tari ya dabeem.”
28Ti Pita lerege en yeti, “Daana, la han sirum dɛna la fum, bo' nuurɛ ti en kiŋɛ ko'om la zuo wa'am fum zi'an na.” 29Ti Yezu yele en yeti, “Wa'ana.” Bala ti Pita ze'ele uureŋɔ la puan pɔhɛ kina ko'om la zuo tɔɔra Yezu. 30Gee en nyɛ sabeeo kãtɛ la, ti dabeem sãɛ en, ti a pɔhɛ muhera, nyaa kaahɛ bahɛ na yeti, “Daana faaɛ mam!” 31Bilam bilam ti Yezu tiɛ a nu'o gurɛ en, gee yele en yeti, “Fum sakerɛ pɔ'ɛ ya, ŋwani ti fum bu'ura?” 32Ban zom uureŋɔ la zuo la, sabeeo la go'e mɛ. 33Ti sɛba en boi uureŋɔ la puan la, na'ahɛ en gee yɛta yeti, “Yelemɛŋerɛ fum sirum dela Yinɛ Dayua.”
Yezu tibɛ Genesarete bã'duma
(Maki 6.53-56)
34Ban yakɛ yakenɛ la, ba kiŋɛ la Genesarete. 35Tiŋa la nɛreba en ta baŋɛ en la, ba muulɛ mɛ kaaɛ tiŋa la, tari bã'duma za'a wa'am a zi'an na, 36gee belum en ti ba kalum a fuo la nɔgbanɛ. Sɛba woo en kalum ku la, nyɛ ba tibega mɛ.

english_text:
The Teaching of the Ancestors
(Mark 7.1-13)
1About this time some Pharisees and teachers of the Law of Moses came from Jerusalem. They asked Jesus, 2“Why don't your disciples obey what our ancestors taught us to do? They don't even wash their hands before they eat.”
3Jesus answered:
Why do you disobey God and follow your own teaching? 4 Didn't God command you to respect your father and mother? Didn't he tell you to put to death all who curse their parents? 5But you let people get by without helping their parents when they should. You let them say that what they have has been offered to God. 6Is this any way to show respect to your parents? You ignore God's commands in order to follow your own teaching. 7And you are nothing but show-offs! Isaiah the prophet was right when he wrote that God had said,
8 “All of you praise me
with your words,
but you never really
think about me.
9It is useless for you
to worship me,
when you teach rules
made up by humans.”
What Really Makes People Unclean
(Mark 7.14-23)
10Jesus called the crowd together and said, “Pay attention and try to understand what I mean. 11The food you put into your mouth doesn't make you unclean and unfit to worship God. The bad words that come out of your mouth are what make you unclean.”
12Then his disciples came over to him and asked, “Do you know you insulted the Pharisees by what you said?”
13Jesus answered, “Every plant that my Father in heaven did not plant will be pulled up by the roots. 14 Stay away from those Pharisees! They are like blind people leading other blind people, and all of them will fall into a ditch.”
15Peter replied, “What did you mean when you talked about the things that make people unclean?”
16Jesus then said:
Don't any of you know by now what I am talking about? 17Don't you know that the food you put into your mouth goes into your stomach and then out of your body? 18 But the words that come out of your mouth come from your heart. And they are what make you unfit to worship God. 19Out of your heart come evil thoughts, murder, unfaithfulness in marriage, vulgar deeds, stealing, telling lies, and insulting others. 20These are what make you unclean. Eating without washing your hands will not make you unfit to worship God.
A Woman's Faith
(Mark 7.24-30)
21Jesus left and went to the territory near the towns of Tyre and Sidon. 22Suddenly a Canaanite woman from there came out shouting, “Lord and Son of David, have pity on me! My daughter is full of demons.” 23Jesus did not say a word. But the woman kept following along and shouting, so his disciples came up and asked him to send her away.
24Jesus said, “I was sent only to the people of Israel! They are like a flock of lost sheep.”
25The woman came closer. Then she knelt down and begged, “Please help me, Lord!”
26Jesus replied, “It isn't right to take food away from children and feed it to dogs.”
27“Lord, this is true,” the woman said, “but even puppies get the crumbs that fall from their owner's table.”
28Jesus answered, “Dear woman, you really do have a lot of faith, and you will be given what you want.” At that moment her daughter was healed.
Jesus Heals Many People
29From there, Jesus went along Lake Galilee. Then he climbed a hill and sat down. 30Large crowds came and brought many people who were paralyzed or blind or lame or unable to talk. They placed them, and many others, in front of Jesus, and he healed them all. 31Everyone was amazed at what they saw and heard. People who had never spoken could now speak. The lame were healed, the paralyzed could walk, and the blind were able to see. Everyone was praising the God of Israel.
Jesus Feeds Four Thousand
(Mark 8.1-10)
32Jesus called his disciples together and told them, “I feel sorry for these people. They have been with me for three days, and they don't have anything to eat. I don't want to send them away hungry. They might faint on their way home.”
33His disciples said, “This place is like a desert. Where can we find enough food to feed such a crowd?”
34Jesus asked them how much food they had. They replied, “Seven small loaves of bread and a few little fish.”
35After Jesus had told the people to sit down, 36he took the seven loaves of bread and the fish and gave thanks. He then broke them and handed them to his disciples, who passed them around to the crowds.
37Everyone ate all they wanted, and the leftovers filled seven large baskets.
38There were 4,000 men who ate, not counting the women and children.
39After Jesus had sent the crowds away, he got into a boat and sailed across the lake. He came to shore near the town of Magadan.
translation_text:
Kiinduma malema
(Maki 7.1-13)
1Pooren ti Farasiiduma la gɔnmi'ineba ze'ele Yerusalɛm wa'am a zi'an na soke en yeti, 2“Ŋwani ti fum zahereba la galum kiinduma malema la? Ba ka peere nu'uhi gee dita.” 3Ti Yezu lerege ba yeti, “Gee ŋwani ti yamam galena Yinɛ pa'alegɔ ya buuri malema zuo? 4Se'ere en sɔi la, Yinɛ yeti, ‘Na'aha fum sɔ la fum ma, fum se'em en tɔgɛ be'em bo' fum sɔ bii fum ma dela fum ki.’ 5Gee yamam yeti, nɛra han yele a sɔ bii a ma yeti, suŋɛ se'ere woo ti fum wan nyɛ ni mam zi'an la, mam dikɛ de bo' la Yinɛ. Bala zuo, nɛre-ina daana ka na'aha a sɔ le yɛ'ɛha. 6Bala, ya buuri malema wa zuo, ti ya ka bihɛ nyɛ Yinɛ yelefum wa. 7Birekɔgehi wa, Azaaya en purɛ ya yele se'em la dela yelemɛŋerɛ. A yeti,
8‘Nɛrebana wa na'ahɛ mam mɛ la ba nɔya,
gee ba suya zaaɛ mɛ la mam,
9Ba pu'uhi mam la yoo,
Ba pa'ali la asaala yɛla gee yeti Yinɛ pa'alegɔ.’ ”
Yelesɛ'a en galeni nɛra
(Maki 7.14-23)
10Ti Yezu yi' nɛrekuuŋɔ la paaɛ a nɛŋan na yele ba yeti, “Kelehe ya, la ya bɔkɛ. 11Dagi sɛla en ki'ire nɛra nuuren en galeni nɛra, gee sɛla en ze'eti a nuuren na.” 12Pooren ti a zahereba la paaɛ en, yele en yeti, “Fum mi ti la daam Farasiiduma la mɛ, ban wum fum yele se'em la?” 13Ti Yezu lerege ba yeti, “Tisɛka ti mam Sɔ en boi saazuo la ka sɛ wan vuuɛ. 14 Bahɛ ya ba ba ma'a, ba dela fɔɔhi en pa'ala fɔɔhi. Fua han data ka tadaana, ba za'a wan lu boko puan.” 15Gee Pita yele en yeti, “Garehɛ makerɛ wa bo' tu.” 16Ti a yeti, “Yamam me kelum ka tara bɔkerɛ? 17Yamam ka nyɛti ti sɛla woo en ni doohe nuurɛ puan kɛ̃ ni sige la puuren ta tole yehe? 18 Gee sɛla en yeheri nuuren na, ze'eti la suure puan na. Dina en galeni nɛra. 19Se'ere en sɔi la, suure la puan ti be'em ti'ihegɔ, nɛrekua, kabohi, yaluntuuma, nageyigum, aze' nyɛ daana pumparema, nɛreba tua zɛ'ɛta na. 20Bana en galeni nɛra, gee a ka pee nu'uhi gee dita ka galeni nɛra.”
Keenan pɔka sakerɛ
(Maki 7.24-30)
21Ti Yezu bahɛ bilam, gee kiŋɛ Taai la Sidɔn sɔ'ɔlum puan. 22Bilam bilam ti Keenan pɔka en ze'ele tinkaŋa mɛa puan yehe na vɔɔla baha na yeti, “Zɔ en nimbu'ɔ, Daana, Deviti dayua wa, en poyua ti kulekpa'bɛ'a tara ka mɛleha.” 23Gee Yezu ka lerege en se'ere. Ti a zahereba la ɛbegɛ en yeti, “Sa'ɛ en ti a kiŋɛ gee a ba' vɔɔla mɛ dɔla tɔ.” 24Ti Yezu lerege yeti, “Ba tum mam la Izirale piihi se'ehi en bɔregɛ la ma'a zi'an na.” 25Gee pɔka wa wa'am me na kpa' duma a nɛŋan, yɛta yeti, “Daana suŋɛ mam.” 26Ti Yezu lerege en yeti, “La dagi ma'a ti n dikɛ kɔma dia lobe bo' baahi.” 27Ti Pɔka la yeti, “Ɛ̃ɛ n Daana, gee baahi la diti di zɔra la en zɔgeri si duma dia zi'an la mɛ.” 28Bilam ti Yezu lerege pɔka wa yeti, “Pɔka wa, fum sakerɛ zo'e ya, la iŋɛ bo' fum wuu fum boti se'em la.” Ti pɔka wa poyua la nyɛ ka tibegɔ bilam bilam.
Yezu tibɛ nɛreba zo'e zo'e
29Yezu en ta bahɛ bilam la, a kiŋɛ doohe la Galilii ateko la, ta zom zoore zuo zi'ire bilam. 30Ti nɛrekuuŋɔ kina a zi'an na, tara wɔbehi, kɔɔrenɔ, fɔɔhi, gɔɔnɔ, la basɛba zo'e zo'e, tari ba na gã'arɛ Yezu nɛŋan, ti a me tibɛ ba. 31Ti la iŋɛ nɛrekuuŋɔ la pakerɛ paaɛ paaɛ, la ban nyɛ gɔɔnɔ en tɔgeri, ti kɔɔrenɔ kina, ti wɔbehi kina, ti fɔɔhi nyɛta. Ti ba pɛgɛra Izirale Yinɛ la.
Tuha anaahi diihego
(Maki 8.1-10)
32Pooren ti Yezu yi' a zahereba la paaɛ a nɛŋan yeti, “Nɛreba wa tari mam la nimbaalega, se'ere en sɔi la, ba boi la mam la dabeha atã en ŋwana gee ka tara sɛla wan di. N ka boti n bahɛ ba ti ba kule la kom. Se'ere en sɔi la, ba ta'am ta lige sore.” 33Ti a zahereba yele en yeti, “Bɛha ti tu wan nyɛ dia zo'e muɔ wa puan diihe nɛrekuuŋɔ kuna taaba wa?” 34Ti Yezu soke ba yeti, “Boroboro ba lɛ ti ya tara?” Ti ba yeti, “Ba yopɔi la zim fii wa.” 35Ti Yezu bo' nɛrekuuŋɔ la nuurɛ ti ba zi'ire tiŋa. 36Ti a to'e boroboro bayopɔi la la zim la. En bo' fara ba'ahɛ la, a fige boroboro la mɛ bo' a zahereba, ti bamam me dikɛ tɔrɛ nɛrekuuŋɔ la. 37Ti ba za'a di ta tigɛ, ti a zahereba la doohe lagehɛ boroboro zɔra la ti ba tigɛ gee bahɛ la, pirɛ pitɔ tuyopɔi. 38Sɛba en di la dela buraahi tuha anaahi, ti kɔma la pɔgehi kãlɛ ka pa'ahɛ. 39En keehe nɛrekuuŋɔ la ba'ahɛ la, a zom la uureŋɔ kiŋɛ Magadan tiŋa.

english_text:
A Demand for a Sign from Heaven
(Mark 8.11-13; Luke 12.54-56)
1 The Pharisees and Sadducees came to Jesus and tried to test him by asking for a sign from heaven. 2He told them:
If the sky is red in the evening, you say the weather will be good. 3But if the sky is red and gloomy in the morning, you say it is going to rain. You can tell what the weather will be like by looking at the sky. But you don't understand what is happening now. 4 You want a sign because you are evil and won't believe! But the only sign you will be given is what happened to Jonah.
Then Jesus left.
The Yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees
(Mark 8.14-21)
5The disciples had forgotten to bring any bread when they crossed the lake. 6 Jesus then warned them, “Watch out! Guard against the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
7The disciples talked this over and said to each other, “He must be saying this because we didn't bring along any bread.”
8Jesus knew what they were thinking and said:
You surely don't have much faith! Why are you talking about not having any bread? 9 Don't you understand? Have you forgotten about the 5,000 people and all those baskets of leftovers from just five loaves of bread? 10 And what about the 4,000 people and all those baskets of leftovers from only seven loaves of bread? 11Don't you know by now that I am not talking to you about bread? Watch out for the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees!
12Finally, the disciples understood that Jesus wasn't talking about the yeast used to make bread, but about the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
Who Is Jesus?
(Mark 8.27-30; Luke 9.18-21)
13When Jesus and his disciples were near the town of Caesarea Philippi, he asked them, “What do people say about the Son of Man?”
14 The disciples answered, “Some people say you are John the Baptist or maybe Elijah or Jeremiah or some other prophet.”
15Then Jesus asked, “But who do you say I am?”
16 Simon Peter spoke up, “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.”
17Jesus told him:
Simon, son of Jonah, you are blessed! You didn't discover this on your own. It was shown to you by my Father in heaven. 18So I will call you Peter, which means “a rock.” On this rock I will build my church, and death itself will not have any power over it. 19 I will give you the keys to the kingdom of heaven, and God in heaven will allow whatever you allow on earth. But he will not allow anything you don't allow.
20Jesus told his disciples not to tell anyone he was the Messiah.
Jesus Speaks about His Suffering and Death
(Mark 8.31—9.1; Luke 9.22-27)
21From then on, Jesus began telling his disciples what would happen to him. He said, “I must go to Jerusalem. There the nation's leaders, the chief priests, and the teachers of the Law of Moses will make me suffer terribly. I will be killed, but three days later I will rise to life.”
22Peter took Jesus aside and told him to stop talking like that. He said, “God would never let this happen to you, Lord!”
23Jesus turned to Peter and said, “Satan, get away from me! You're in my way because you think like everyone else and not like God.”
24 Then Jesus said to his disciples:
If any of you want to be my followers, you must forget about yourself. You must take up your cross and follow me. 25 If you want to save your life, you will destroy it. But if you give up your life for me, you will find it. 26What will you gain, if you own the whole world but destroy yourself? What would you give to get back your soul?
27 The Son of Man will soon come in the glory of his Father and with his angels to reward all people for what they have done. 28I promise you some of those standing here will not die before they see the Son of Man coming with his kingdom.
translation_text:
Daalehum eere
(Maki 8.11-13; Luki 12.54-56)
1 Farasii la Sadusiiduma la wa'am na ti ba makɛ la Yezu bihɛ. Nyaa yele en yeti, iŋɛ daalehum en ze'ele saazuo na. 2Ti Yezu lerege ba yeti, “Yinɛ han ma'ɛ, ya ni yeti, ‘Zina dela dabehesunɛ, se'ere en la sɔi la, sagbama la mu'ɛ mɛ.’ 3Ti bulika me, ya wan yeti, ‘Sabeeo wan lobe zina se'ere en sɔi la, sagbama la mu'ɛ mɛ gee bɔta saa.’ Ya mi' sagbama yɛla pa'ala, gee ya kan ta'am pa'alɛ saŋa woo daalehum en de se'em. 4 Be'em la tuunfi'iha buuri saŋa en eere daalehum. Gee daalehum ka boi en wan bo' ba han dagena Yona daalehum la ma'a.” Ti a bahɛ ba gee kiŋɛ.
Farasii la Sadusii dabelɛ
(Maki 8.14-21)
5Yezu zahereba la en yakɛ ateko la yakenɛ deyima ha la, ba tamɛ mɛ ka tara dia. 6 Ti Yezu yele ba yeti, “Tara ya mɛhi suŋa, gee la ya mina Farasii la Sadusiiduma dabelɛ la yele.” 7Ti ba yɛta taaba yeti, “Tumam en ka tari dia na la en sɔi ti a tɔgera bala.” 8Yezu en mi' ba puti'irɛ la, ti a yele ba yeti, yamam asakerɛ pɔ'ɛ ya duma wa, “Ŋwani ti ya tɔgera ya ka tari dia na yele? 9 Yamam kelum ka bɔkera? Yamam ka tɛri boroboro banuu la n daa diihe nɛreba tuha anuu la, la pitɔ se'em ti ya daa doohe va pirɛ la? 10 Bii boroboro bayopɔi ti n daa dikɛ diihe tuha anaahi la, la pitɔ se'em ti ya daa doohe va pirɛ la? 11Ŋwani ti ya koŋe ya bɔkɛ ti n ka tɔgeri dia yele? Mini ya Farasii la Sadusiiduma la dabelɛ la yele!” 12Bala ti ba nyaa bɔkɛ ti a ka yeti ba ba tara mɛhi suŋa, dabelɛ la yele, gee Farasii la Sadusiiduma la pa'alegɔ la.
Pita pa'alɛ Yezu en de se'em
(Maki 8.27-30; Luki 9.18-21)
13Yezu en paaɛ Kasariya Filipi tiŋa puan ba'ahɛ la, ti a nyaa soke a zahereba la yeti, “Nɛreba yeti mam Asaala Dayua wa dela ani?” 14 Ti ba yeti, “Sɛba yeti fum dela Yɔn Ko'sɔɔra la, ti sɛba me yeti fum dela Eliya, ti basɛba mɛ kelum yeti fum dela Yɛremiya bii nɔtɔgeheba la ayima.” 15Ti a yele ba yeti, “Gee yamam yeti mam dela ani?” 16 Ti Simɔn Pita lerege yeti, “Fum n de Kiresta la, Yinɛ vua la Dayua.” 17Ti Yezu lerege en yeti, “Sum boi mɛ la hɔ Simɔn, Yona dayua wa. Se'ere en sɔi la, dagi ingɔŋɔ la ziim n lilege dina wa bo' fum, gee mam Sɔ se'em en boi saazuo ha. 18N yeti fum, fum dela Pita, tankana wa zuo ti mam wan mɛ en pu'uhegɔ yire la, ti kum paŋa kan malum nyaŋɛ dɛ. 19N wan bo' fum saazuo sɔ'ɔlum la kparehi, sɛla woo ti fum bobe tiŋa wa zuo, saazuo ha me wan bobe. Sɛla wuu ti fum lorege bahɛ tiŋa wa zuo, saazuo ha me wan lorege bahɛ.” 20Ti a kagɛ a zahereba la paaɛ paaɛ ti ba da yele nɛra nɛra ti eŋa n da Kiresta la.
Yezu ti'ele yele a kum, la a vo'ore
(Maki 8.31—9.1; Luki 9.22-27)
21Sankaŋa puan yɛ'a ha, ti Yezu pɔhɛ yɛta a zahereba la yeti, la dela kiŋɛ Yerusalɛm ta namehɛ namehekãtɛ kiinduma la, malema kiinduma duma la gɔnmi'ineba la nu'uhen, gee ti ba ku' en. Gee dabeha atã daarɛ a wan vo'e a kum la puan. 22Ti Pita kɔkɛ Yezu lebe kinkɛleŋa ta ɔbera a tuba ti a da tɔgera bala. Yinɛ gu'. “Daana! Dina kan malum paaɛ ya.” 23Gee Yezu ŋmɛregɛ yele Pita yeti, “Fɔregɛ mam zi'an Sagena wa. Fum dela pirega pita mam, se'ere en sɔi la, fum puti'irɛ ka boi saazuo yɛla puan, gee asaala yɛla puan.”
Pumpuuredɔɔ la namehegɔ
24 Ti Yezu yele a zahereba la yeti, “Se'em woo en boti a dɔla mam, a daana zagehɛ a mɛŋa gee dikɛ a pumpuuredɔɔ zi dɔla mam. 25 Se'ere en sɔi la, se'em en boti a gu' a vom, wan bɔregɛ bɔ bahɛ. Ti se'em me en bɔregɛ a vom mam zuo, wan nyɛ bɔ. 26Beni nyuurɔ ti a wan nyɛ, a han nyɛ tiŋa wa lɔgerɔ za'a gee koŋe a nyɔvore? Bii a wan dikɛ la beni ta'am tee ba nyɔvore?
27 “Se'ere en sɔi la, Asaala dayua la yeti a wa'am me na la a suŋereba, a Sɔ suŋa la puan, bilam ti a wan yɔ nɛrawoo doohe en tum se'em. 28Yelemɛŋerɛ ti n yɛta ya wa, ti basɛba boi yan ze' wa puan kan lem kum, gee wan nyɛ Asaala Dayua la kinɛ a sɔ'ɔlum la puan na.”

english_text:
The True Glory of Jesus
(Mark 9.2-13; Luke 9.28-36)
1 Six days later Jesus took Peter and the brothers James and John with him. They went up on a very high mountain where they could be alone. 2There in front of the disciples, Jesus was completely changed. His face was shining like the sun, and his clothes became white as light.
3All at once Moses and Elijah were there talking with Jesus. 4So Peter said to him, “Lord, it is good for us to be here! Let us make three shelters, one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
5 While Peter was still speaking, the shadow of a bright cloud passed over them. From the cloud a voice said, “This is my own dear Son, and I am pleased with him. Listen to what he says!” 6When the disciples heard the voice, they were so afraid they fell flat on the ground. 7But Jesus came over and touched them. He said, “Get up and don't be afraid!” 8When they opened their eyes, they saw only Jesus.
9On their way down from the mountain, Jesus warned his disciples not to tell anyone what they had seen until after the Son of Man had been raised from death.
10 The disciples asked Jesus, “Don't the teachers of the Law of Moses say Elijah must come before the Messiah does?”
11 Jesus told them, “Elijah certainly will come and get everything ready. 12 In fact, he has already come. But the people did not recognize him and treated him just as they wanted to. They will soon make the Son of Man suffer in the same way.” 13Then the disciples understood Jesus was talking to them about John the Baptist.
Jesus Heals a Boy
(Mark 9.14-29; Luke 9.37-43a)
14Jesus and his disciples returned to the crowd. A man knelt in front of him 15and said, “Lord, have pity on my son! He has a bad case of epilepsy and often falls into a fire or into water. 16I brought him to your disciples, but none of them could heal him.”
17Jesus said, “You people are too stubborn to have any faith! How much longer must I be with you? Why do I have to put up with you? Bring the boy here.” 18Then Jesus spoke sternly to the demon. It went out of the boy, and right then he was healed.
19Later the disciples went to Jesus in private and asked him, “Why couldn't we force out the demon?”
20-21 Jesus replied:
It is because you don't have enough faith! But I can promise you this. If you had faith no larger than a mustard seed, you could tell this mountain to move from here to there. And it would. Everything would be possible for you.
Jesus Again Speaks about His Death
(Mark 9.30-32; Luke 9.43b-45)
22While Jesus and his disciples were going from place to place in Galilee, he told them, “The Son of Man will be handed over to people 23who will kill him. But three days later he will rise to life.” All of this made the disciples very sad.
Paying the Temple Tax
24 When Jesus and the others arrived in Capernaum, the collectors for the temple tax came to Peter and asked, “Does your teacher pay the temple tax?”
25“Yes, he does,” Peter answered.
After they had returned home, Jesus went up to Peter and asked him, “Simon, what do you think? Do the kings of this earth collect taxes and fees from their own people or from foreigners?”
26Peter answered, “From foreigners.”
Jesus replied, “Then their own people don't have to pay. 27But we don't want to cause trouble. So go cast a line into the lake and pull out the first fish you hook. Open its mouth, and you will find a coin. Use it to pay your taxes and mine.”
translation_text:
Yezu teere
(Maki 9.2-13; Luki 9.28-36)
1 Dabeha ayoobe n tole, Ti Yezu doohe la Pita, Yemesi la a suuɔ Yɔn zom zoore zuin zuin ha ba ma'a. 2Ti Yezu iŋa ta tee ba nɛŋan, ti a nɛŋa nyakera wuu wuntɛɛŋa la, ti a lɔgerɔ pelege kirikiri. 3Ba yeti ba bihɛ ti Moose la Eliya n bala niiɛ na zɛ'a la ba, tɔgera la Yezu. 4Ti Pita yele Yezu yeti, “N daana, ka'lam bɔŋa ani suŋa. Fum han bɔta, mam wan ti' suga atã ka'lam, fum deyima, Moose deyima, Eliya me deyima.” 5 En boi bini tɔgera la, ti sagbanɛ en nyagere n bala wa'am na pi' ba. Ti kua ze'ele sagbanɛ la puan tɔgɛ bahɛ na yeti, “Mam dayua n ŋwana, se'em ti mam nɔŋɛ paaɛ paaɛ. Mam nini n tigɛ la se'em n bala, kɛleha ya en.” 6A zahereba la en wum ŋwana la, ba lu la tiŋa ti dabeem sãɛ ba. 7Ti Yezu wa'am na kalum ba gee yeti, “Ihege ya, de tara ya dabeem.” 8Ban gorege bihɛ la, ba ka nyɛ nɛra nɛra gee Yezu a ma'a.
9Ban ze'ele zoore la zuo sigera na la, ti Yezu kagɛ ba yeti, “Da yele ya nɛra nɛra lilegere wa, ta paaɛ hansɛka ti Asaala Dayua la ta ihege a kum la puan.” 10Ti a zahereba la soke en yeti, “Ŋwani ti gɔnmi'ineba la yeti, Eliya n wan wa'am yia na?” 11Ti a lerege ba yeti, “Eliya sirum kini na, a wan bahɛ ti sɛla wuu lebe ze'ele suŋa. 12 Gee mam yeti ya yeti, Eliya pugum wa'am me na, gee ba ka baŋɛ en, gee iŋɛ en ban boti se'em. Bala mɛa ti Asaala Dayua la me yeti a nyɛ namehegɔ ba nu'uhen.” 13Ŋwana ti a zahereba la bɔkɛ ti a tɔgeri la Yɔn Ko'sɔɔra la yele.
Yezu tibɛ budibela
(Maki 9.14-29; Luki 9.37-43a)
14Ban paaɛ nɛrekuuŋɔ la zi'an la, buraa en paaɛ a zi'an na, kpa' duma a nɛŋan, 15gee yeti, “N Daana, zɔ n dayua wa nimbu'ɔ, se'ere en sɔi la, a luti la kilenki'ire. A nameheri mɛ paaɛ paaɛ. A ni ta'am ta lu bugum puan mɛ, bii a lu ko'om puan. 16Ti mam tari en wa'am fum zahereba la zi'an na, gee ba ka nyaŋɛ tibɛ en.” 17Ti Yezu lerege yeti, “Yamam akatare sakerɛ, la ŋmɛlema buuri wa, mam yeti n bɔna la ya yuue la ŋwani? Mam yeti n ŋmibe la ya ta paaɛ la ŋwani? Tari ya en wa'am ka'lam na bo' mam.” 18Ti Yezu tahɛ kulekpa'bɛ'a la, ti ka yehe a puan, ti bia la nyɛ ka tibegɔ bilam bilam. 19Pooren ti a zahereba la wa'am a zi'an na ba ma'a, soke en yeti, “Ŋwani ti tumam ka ta'am sa'ɛ kulekpa'bɛ'a la ti ka yehe?” 20 Ti a yele ba yeti, “Ya sakerɛ la en pɔ'ɛ la en sɔi. Yelemɛŋerɛ ti en yɛta ya wa, ti ya han tara sakerɛ ti de zuna la nangembiileho, ya wan yele zoore yeti, ‘Vuuɛ ka'lam,’ ti de sirum vuuɛ, ti sɛla ka bɔna wan kpe'em bo' ya.” 21[Gee kulekpa'bɛ'a kana taaba kan yehe, han dagena pu'uhegɔ la nɔlurɛ ma'a.]
22Yezu la a zahereba la en ta lagehɛ Galilii la, ti Yezu yele ba yeti, “Ba wan koohe Asaala Dayua wa bo' iŋɛ saaleba nu'uhen, 23ti ba ku' en, gee dabeha atã daarɛ a wan vo'e.” Ti a zahereba la suya sagum paaɛ paaɛ.
Pu'uhegɔ yire Kuba yɛla
24 Paaɛ Kapɛnum la, ti sɛba en to'ohe pu'uhegɔ yire kuba la wa'am Pita zi'an na yeti, “Yamam pa'ala la ka lagum yɔɔra pu'uhegɔ yire kuba la bii?” 25Ti Pita yeti, “Ɛ̃ɛ, a yɔɔri.” Ti ban ta kule yire na la, Yezu tɔgɛ la yele deni yia, soke yeti, “Fum ti'ihɛ la dinɛ Simɔn? Tiŋa wa zuo na'duma to'ohe kuba la bani zi'an? Ba mɛhi kɔma bii saama?” 26Ti Pita yele en yeti, “Saama zi'an” ti Yezu yeti, “La han dɛna bala, ba kɔma la yi boi la fai. 27Gee tumam en ka boti tu zeem ba la zuo, kiŋɛ mɔgeren ta lobe zim baŋa, zim sebo ti fum nyɔkɛ yia la, fum han ya'ɛ bu nuurɛ, fum wan nyɛ lagekɔberɛ. Dikɛ bumɔ ta bo' ba, ti la dɛna fum la mam en bala.”

english_text:
Who Is the Greatest?
(Mark 9.33-37; Luke 9.46-48)
1 About this time the disciples came to Jesus and asked him who would be the greatest in the kingdom of heaven. 2Jesus called for a child to come over and stand near him. 3 Then he said:
I promise you this. If you don't change and become like a child, you will never get into the kingdom of heaven. 4But if you are as humble as this child, you are the greatest in the kingdom of heaven. 5And when you welcome one of these children because of me, you welcome me.
Temptations To Sin
(Mark 9.42-48; Luke 17.1,2)
6It will be terrible for people who cause even one of my little followers to sin. Those people would be better off thrown into the deepest part of the ocean with a heavy stone tied around their necks! 7The world is in for trouble because of the way it causes people to sin. There will always be something to cause people to sin, but anyone who does this will be in for trouble.
8 If your hand or foot causes you to sin, chop it off and throw it away! You would be better off to go into life paralyzed or lame than to have two hands or two feet and be thrown into the fire that never goes out. 9 If your eye causes you to sin, poke it out and get rid of it. You would be better off to go into life with only one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fires of hell.
The Lost Sheep
(Luke 15.3-7)
10-11 Don't be cruel to any of these little ones! I promise you their angels are always with my Father in heaven. 12Let me ask you this. What would you do if you had 100 sheep and one of them wandered off? Wouldn't you leave the 99 on the hillside and go look for the one that had wandered away? 13I am sure that finding it would make you happier than having the 99 that never wandered off. 14That's how it is with your Father in heaven. He doesn't want any of these little ones to be lost.
When Someone Sins
(Luke 17.3)
15 If one of my followers sins against you, go and point out what was wrong. But do it in private, just between the two of you. If that person listens, you have won back a follower. 16 But if that one refuses to listen, take along one or two others. The Scriptures teach that every complaint must be proven true by two or more witnesses. 17If the follower refuses to listen to them, report the matter to the church. Anyone who refuses to listen to the church must be treated like an unbeliever or a tax collector.
Allowing and Not Allowing
18 I promise you God in heaven will allow whatever you allow on earth, but God will not allow anything you don't allow. 19I promise that when any two of you on earth agree about something you are praying for, my Father in heaven will do it for you. 20Whenever two or three of you come together in my name, I am there with you.
An Official Who Refused To Forgive
21 Peter came up to the Lord and asked, “How many times should I forgive someone who does something wrong to me? Is seven times enough?”
22 Jesus answered:
Not just 7 times, but 77 times! 23This story will show you what the kingdom of heaven is like:
One day a king decided to call in his officials and ask them to give an account of what they owed him. 24As he was doing this, one official was brought in who owed him 50,000,000 silver coins. 25But he didn't have any money to pay what he owed. The king ordered him to be sold, along with his wife and children and all he owned, in order to pay the debt.
26The official got down on his knees and began begging, “Have pity on me, and I will pay you every cent I owe!” 27The king felt sorry for him and let him go free. He even told the official that he did not have to pay back the money.
28But as this official was leaving, he happened to meet another official, who owed him 100 silver coins. So he grabbed the man by the throat. He started choking him and said, “Pay me what you owe!”
29The man got down on his knees and began begging, “Have pity on me, and I will pay you back.” 30But the first official refused to have pity. Instead, he went and had the other official put in jail until he could pay what he owed.
31When some other officials found out what had happened, they felt sorry for the man who had been put in jail. Then they told the king what had happened. 32The king called the first official back in and said, “You're an evil man! When you begged for mercy, I said you did not have to pay back a cent. 33Don't you think you should show pity to someone else, as I did to you?” 34The king was so angry that he ordered the official to be tortured until he could pay back everything he owed. 35That is how my Father in heaven will treat you, if you don't forgive each of my followers with all your heart.
translation_text:
Se'em en gani za'a
(Maki 9.33-37; Luki 9.46-48)
1 Sankaŋa ti Yezu zahereba la wa'am a zi'an na soke en yeti, “Ani en gani za'a saazuo sɔ'ɔlum la puan?” 2Ti a yi' bia na ze'ele ba nɛŋan, 3 ti a yeti, “N yeti ya la Yelemɛŋerɛ, ti han dagena ya tee mɛ ana wuu kɔma, ya kan malum kɛ̃' saazuo sɔ'ɔlum la puan. 4Se'em woo en sigehe a mɛa wuu bia wa, n de se'em n gani za'a saazuo sɔ'ɔlum la puan. 5Se'em woo n to'e bia n ani woo ŋwana mam yu'urɛ zuo, to'e la mam.
Be'em pã'ahegɔ
(Maki 9.42-48; Luki 17.1, 2)
6“Ya se'em han dikɛ pirega lɔkɔ beŋe ti la pirɛ bumbibehi wa ayima en sakɛ bo' mam wa, la wan ana suŋa bo' a daana ti ba dikɛ nɛɛrɛ kugekãtɛ lu' yule a yugela tari en ta za'ɛ bahɛ ko'omen ti a muhi sige tiŋa tiŋa ha. 7Yele boi tiŋa wa zuo, la sɛla en piti nɛreba lubera n boi ka zuo la. Yele sɛ'a en piti nɛreba lubera wan ba'afum wa'am me na, gee yele boi fum se'em daana zuo ti pirega lɔkɔ wa wan ze'ele na la.
8 “Fum nu'o bii na'arɛ han bahɛ ti fum pita luta, ŋmaaɛ bahɛ, la wan ana suŋa bo' fum ti fum kɛ̃ vom puan la nu'yiŋɔ la na'yinɛ nyana fum tara nu'uhi siyi bii nama ayi' gee ti ba dikɛ fum bahɛ bugum sebo n ka diti kiŋera la puan. 9 Fum niho han bahɛ ti fum pita luta, kpikɛ bu lobe bahɛ, la wan ana suŋa bo' fum ti fum ta kɛ̃' vom puan la ninyimɔ nyana fum tara nini iyi' gee ti ba ta dikɛ fum lobe bahɛ bugum tiŋa.
Pehego n bɔregɛ makerɛ
(Luki 15.3-7)
10“Bihɛ ya suŋa la ya da bihɛ bumbibehi wa ayima yoo. Mam yeti ya mɛ wa, ti saazuo ha, ba suŋereba saŋa woo kɔ'ɔm nyɛta mam Sɔ en boi saazuo nɛŋa mɛ saŋa woo. 11[Se'ere en sɔi la, Asaala Dayua wa wa'am na ti a faaɛ la sɛba n bɔregɛ la bahɛ Diimen diimen gulehɛgɔ tuseto ka tari ze'kana]. 12Yamam ti'ihɛ la deni? Nɛra han tara piihi kɔbega, ti kuyima bɔregɛ, a kan bahɛ pihiwai' la siwai' la zoore zuo gee ɛ peseko en bɔregɛ la me yoi? 13La han iŋɛ nyɛ kɔ, yelemɛŋerɛ ti n yɛta ya wa, ti a puurɛ wan pee mɛ, la peyiŋɔ la, gana piihi pihiwai' la siwai' la en ka bɔregɛ la. 14Bala mɛa ti, la dagena ya Sɔ n boi saazuo ha la puti'irɛ ti bumbibehi wa ayima bɔregɛ.
15 “Se'em han bɔna lageŋɔ puan han tuue fum, pa'alɛ en a tuure la, fum la eŋa ma'a tiŋasuka. A han kelehe fum, fum nyaŋɛ fum suuɔ la lebe me na en bala. 16 Gee a han ka kelehe fum, doohe la nɛra ayima bii bayi' pa'ahɛ fum puan, ti yetɔgesebo woo ti ya wan tɔgɛ la, nɛreba bayi' batã wan dɛna aze' nyɛ duma yeti bumɔ n bala. 17Gee a han zagehɛ ka kelehe bamam, yele lageŋɔ la, ti se'em n tuue wa han kelum zagehɛ ti a pun kan kelehe lageŋɔ la, iŋɛ ya nɛre-ina daana wuu se'em en ka zoti Yezu, bii kubetɔ'ɔha la. 18Yelemɛŋerɛ ti n yɛta ya wa, ti sɛla woo ti ya lu' tiŋa wa zuo, saazuo ha me wan lu'. Sɛla woo ti ya lorege bahɛ tiŋa wa zuo, saazuo ha wan me wan lorege bahɛ. 19Le yɛ'ɛha, yelemɛŋerɛ ti en yɛta ya wa, ya bayi' han ku nuurɛ tiŋa wa zuo doohe la sɛla woo ti ya soke bɔta, mam Sɔ n boi saazuo la wan tum dɛ bo' ya. 20Se'ere en sɔi la, zi'an ti nɛreba ba yi' ba tã lagum taaba mam yu'urɛ puan, mam boi bini mɛ la ba.”
Sugeri dia
21 Ti Pita paaɛ Yezu nɛŋan soke en yeti, “Daana, se'em n suuɔ han tuue mam, sugum nuuren bulɛ ti n wan di sugeri bo' en? La tara tara ta paaɛ woo sugum nuuren buyopɔi?” 22 Ti Yezu yele en yeti, “Dagi sugum nuuren buyopɔi ma'a, gee mam yeti fum la yelemɛŋerɛ wa, sugum nuuren pihiyopɔi sugum nuurɛ buyopɔi.”
23“Dina wa zuo, saazuo sɔ'ɔlum la dikɛ makɛ mɛ la naba en yeti a baŋɛ a yamehi tuuma en kini se'em. 24En pɔhɛ viihegɔ la, ayima tari la a hanɛ la ligeri en de talenta tuha pia, ti ba tari en wa'am na. 25Gee yameŋa wa n kan nyaŋɛ yɔ hanɛ la zuo, ti a daana wa bo' nuurɛ ti ba koohe en la a pɔga, la a kɔma, la lɔgerɔ yɔ hanɛ la. 26Ti yameŋa wa pɔrɛ nama a daana wa nɛŋan ŋmɛ'ɛra nupu'ɔ gee na'aha a daana la yɛta yeti, ‘Iŋɛ sugeri bo' mam, gee n wan yɔ sɛla woo.’ 27Ti nimbu'ɔ nyɔkɛ yameŋa wa daana la, ti a bahɛ en, gee di sugeri bo' a hanɛ la bo' en. 28Gee yameŋa kana mɛa wa en yehe na la, a wa'am na nyɛ la a yameŋa tadaana kayima n me tari a hanɛ dinaari kɔbega, ti a kɔ'ɔm gurɛ a kunkore kɛgera gee yeti ‘Yɔ mam n hanɛ la.’ 29Ti a yameŋa tadaana wa pɔrɛ nama a nɛŋan ŋmɛ'ɛra nu'pu'ɔ yɛta en yeti, ‘Iŋɛ sugeri bo' mam gee en wan yɔ hɔ.’ 30Gee a kɔ'ɔm mum la nini zagehɛ, gee tari en ta pagɛ ti a yɔ hanɛ la za'a. 31Naba la yamehi sise'ehi n nyɛ sɛla n iŋɛ la, ba suya n sagum paaɛ paaɛ, ti ba kiŋɛ ta yele ba daana la sɛla n iŋɛ. 32Bala, ti a daana la yi' en na yele en yeti, ‘Putɔya wa, mam bahɛ fum hanɛ la za'a bo' fum mɛ fum pɔri nama ŋmɛ nupu'ɔ la zuo. 33Fum me ka suni ni ti fum zɔ fum yameŋa tadaana wa nimbu'ɔ, wuu mam zɔ fum nimbu'ɔ se'em la?’ 34Ti a daana la dikɛ susutuulɛ, dikɛ en bo' ti ba namehɛ en ta paaɛ hansɛka ti a wan yɔ hanɛ la za'a za'a. 35Ŋwana ti mam Sɔ en boi saazuo ha me wan dikɛ iŋɛ ya, ya se'em han ka di sugeri bo' a suuɔ a suure puan.”

english_text:
Teaching about Divorce
(Mark 10.1-12)
1When Jesus finished teaching, he left Galilee and went to the part of Judea east of the Jordan River. 2Large crowds followed him, and he healed their sick.
3Some Pharisees wanted to test Jesus. They came up to him and asked, “Is it right for a man to divorce his wife for just any reason?”
4 Jesus answered, “Don't you know in the beginning the Creator made a man and a woman? 5 That's why a man leaves his father and mother and gets married. He becomes like one person with his wife. 6Then they are no longer two people, but one. And no one should separate a couple God has joined together.”
7 The Pharisees asked Jesus, “Why did Moses say a man could write out divorce papers and send his wife away?”
8Jesus replied, “You are so heartless! That's why Moses allowed you to divorce your wife. But from the beginning God did not intend it to be that way. 9 I say if your wife has not committed some terrible sexual sin, you must not divorce her to marry someone else. If you do, you are unfaithful.”
10The disciples said, “If that's how it is between a man and a woman, it's better not to get married.”
11Jesus told them, “Only those people who have been given the gift of staying single can accept this teaching. 12Some people are unable to marry because of birth defects or because of what someone has done to their bodies. Others stay single in order to serve God better. Anyone who can accept this teaching should do so.”
Jesus Blesses Little Children
(Mark 10.13-16; Luke 18.15-17)
13Some people brought their children to Jesus, so he could place his hands on them and pray for them. His disciples told the people to stop bothering him. 14But Jesus said, “Let the children come to me, and don't try to stop them! People who are like these children belong to God's kingdom.” 15After Jesus had placed his hands on the children, he left.
A Rich Young Man
(Mark 10.17-31; Luke 18.18-30)
16A man came to Jesus and asked, “Teacher, what good thing must I do to have eternal life?”
17Jesus said to him, “Why do you ask me about what is good? Only God is good. If you want to have eternal life, you must obey his commandments.”
18 “Which ones?” the man asked.
Jesus answered, “Do not murder. Be faithful in marriage. Do not steal. Do not tell lies about others. 19 Respect your father and mother. And love others as much as you love yourself.” 20The young man said, “I have obeyed all of these. What else must I do?”
21Jesus replied, “If you want to be perfect, go sell everything you own! Give the money to the poor, and you will have riches in heaven. Then come and be my follower.” 22When the young man heard this, he went away sad, because he was very rich.
23Jesus said to his disciples, “I tell you, it's terribly hard for rich people to get into the kingdom of heaven! 24In fact, it's easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to get into God's kingdom.”
25When the disciples heard this, they were greatly surprised and asked, “How can anyone ever be saved?”
26Jesus looked straight at them and said, “There are some things people cannot do, but God can do anything.”
27Peter replied, “Remember, we have left everything to be your followers! What will we get?”
28 Jesus answered:
Yes, all of you have become my followers. And so in the future world, when the Son of Man sits on his glorious throne, I promise you will sit on twelve thrones to judge the twelve tribes of Israel. 29All who have given up home or brothers and sisters or father and mother or children or land for me will be given 100 times as much. They will also have eternal life. 30 But many who are now first will be last, and many who are last will be first.
translation_text:
Pɔgelebehego la sire bahega
(Maki 10.1-12)
1Yezu en tɔgɛ yele ana ba'ahɛ la, a bahɛ Galilii mɛ gee kiŋɛ Yudiya n boi Yɔɔdan yakenɛ ha la. 2Ti Nɛrekuuŋɔ doohe a poore, ti a tibɛ ba bilam.
3Ti Farasii basɛba wa'am a zi'an na, ban boti ba makɛ en bihɛ la, ti ba soke en yeti, “La de ma'a, ti buraa lebehe a pɔga yele se'ere puan?” 4 Ti Yezu lebehe ba yeti, “Yamam ka kãalɛ lan gulehɛ yeti ‘Se'em en naam ba pi'ileŋo puan na la naam ba la buraa la pɔka.’ 5 Gee le yeti, ‘Dina wa zuo la, buraa wan bahɛ ka sɔ la ka ma gee naaɛ la a pɔga, ti ba bayi' la dɛna inganɛ deyina’? 6Bala, ba ka le dɛna bayi', ba nyaa dela inganɛ deyina. Bala, sɛla ti Yinɛ dikɛ naaɛ taaba, nɛra de welege.” 7 Ti ba yele en yeti, “Gee ŋwani ti Moose bo' tu nuurɛ ti tu ta'am bo' ka sa'arɛ gɔŋɔ gee nyaa lebehe ka?” 8Ti Yezu yele ba yeti, “Ya sukãberɛ la zuo ti Moose bo' ya sore ti ya lɛbeha ya pɔgeba, gee pi'ileŋo puan na la, la dagi bala. 9 Gee n yeti ya mɛ wa, ti se'em woo en lebehe a pɔga han gee tee di pɔga han dagi ka galum mɛ zuo, tum la kabohi.”
10Ti Yezu zahereba la yele en yeti, “La han dɛna bala sira la pɔga tiŋasuka, la ye ani suŋa ti nɛra da di pɔga bii ele sira.” 11Gee Yezu yele ba yeti, “Dagi nɛra woo en wan ta'am to'e pa'ali kuna wa, gee sɛba ma'a ti Yinɛ dikɛ pa'ali kuna bo' ba la. 12Se'ere en sɔi la, sɛba kɔ'ɔm dɛna la bula ba maduma puuren na, ti sɛba me dɛna bula doohe la nɛreba en iŋɛ ba, ti sɛba me iŋɛ ba mɛhi dɛna bula saazuo sɔ'ɔlum la zuo. Se'em n wan ta'am bɔkɛ yele dina wa la, a bɔkɛ.”
Yezu iŋɛ kɔma sum
(Maki 10.13-16; Luki 18.15-17)
13Pooren ti ba tari kɔmbibehi wa'am a zi'an na, ti a dikɛ a nu'uhi pagelɛ ba zuo pu'uhɛ bo' ba. Ti Yezu zahereba la tahera sɛba en tari kɔma la wa'am na la. 14Gee Yezu yele ba yeti, “Bahɛ ya ti kɔma la wa'am n zi'an na. Da gu'uri ya ba, se'ere en sɔi la, sɛba en ani wuu kɔma wa la, n sɔi saazuo sɔ'ɔlum la.” 15Gee nyaa dikɛ a nu'uhi pagelɛ kɔma la zuto gee kiŋɛ.
16Bilam bilam ti nɛra ayima wa'am a zi'an na yeti, “Pa'ala, itesuŋɔ kuni ti en wan tum tara vom kamba'ahɛ?” 17Ti Yezu yele en yeti, “Ŋwani ti fum sɔkera mam ti sum yele? Nɛra ayima ma'a n de suŋa. Fum han bɔta ti fum kɛ̃' vom puan, gurɛ nɔze'elego la suŋa suŋa.” 18 Ti a soke en yeti, “Aŋa bɛɛ?” Ti Yezu yele en yeti, “Fum da ku ka'ɛ ziim Fum da tum kabohi, fum da zu, Fum da dɛna aze' nyɛ pumparema, 19 Na'aha fum sɔ la fum ma; gee me nɔŋɛ hɔ mabia wuu fum nɔŋɛ fum mɛŋa se'em la.” 20Gee budibele paalega wa yele Yezu yeti, “Mam pun ita yele ana za'a mɛ n biilemen na; beni ti en kelum gee?” 21Ti Yezu yele en yeti, “Fum nyaa han bɔta ti fum bi'ɛ kahegɛ, nyaa kiŋɛ ta koohe fum lɔgerɔ la, dikɛ ligeri la bo' naheduma, ti fum tarega la nyaa bɔna saazuo ha, gee ti fum nyaa wa'am na dɔla mam.” 22Bumbile-paalega wa n wum ŋwana la, a kiŋɛ mɛ la susageŋɔ, se'ere en sɔi la, a ba' pãrɛ mɛ.
23Ti Yezu nyaa yele a zahereba la yeti, “Yelemɛŋerɛ ti n yɛta ya wa, ti la wan kpe'em mɛ bo' buntata ti a kɛ̃' saazuo sɔ'ɔlum la puan. 24N le yele pa'ahɛ, la de naana bo' yugenɛ ti de doohe fupiho yoko puan tole, gana buntata kɛ̃' Yinɛ sɔ'ɔlum la puan.” 25A zahereba la n wum dina wa la, la iŋɛ ba la pakerɛ paaɛ paaɛ, ti ba yeti, “Ani n yi wan nyɛ faarɛ?” 26Ti Yezu bihɛ ba, gee yeti, “Saaleba zi'an la kan ta'am tum. Gee Yinɛ zi'an sɛla woo wan ta'am tum.”
27Ŋwana ti Pita lerege Yezu yeti, “Bihɛ, tumam bahɛ sɛla woo mɛ gee dɔla la fum. Beni nyuurɔ ti tu wan nyɛ de puan?” 28 Ti Yezu yele ba yeti, “N yeti ya la Yelemɛŋerɛ wa ti, sɛla woo paalega saŋa la han ta paaɛ, ti Asaala Dayua la zi'ire a suŋa na'am kuka la zuo ba'ahɛ, yamam sɛba en doohe mam la me wan zi'a na'am kugehi pia la tuyi' me bihera Izirale buuri pia la ba yi' la. 29Se'em woo n bahɛ yiya, suurɔ, bii tapa, sɔ bii ma, kɔma, bii vatɔ mam yu'urɛ wa zuo, wan lebehe nyɛ ba kɔbehi, gee me wan to'e vom kamba'ahɛ. 30 Gee sɛba zo'e zo'e en diŋɛ nɛŋa, wan ta yee pooren ti sɛba en yee pooren ta diŋɛ nɛŋa.

english_text:
Workers in a Vineyard
1As Jesus was telling what the kingdom of heaven would be like, he said:
Early one morning a man went out to hire some workers for his vineyard. 2After he had agreed to pay them the usual amount for a day's work, he sent them off to his vineyard.
