1The Law of Moses is like a shadow of the good things to come. This shadow isn't the good things themselves, because it cannot free people from sin by the sacrifices offered year after year. 2If there were worshipers who already have their sins washed away and their consciences made clear, there would not be any need to go on offering sacrifices. 3-4But the blood of bulls and goats cannot take away sins. It only reminds people of their sins from one year to the next.
5 When Christ came into the world, he said to God,
“Sacrifices and offerings
are not what you want,
but you have given me
my body.
6No, you are not pleased
with animal sacrifices
and offerings for sin.”
7Then Christ said,
“And so, my God,
I have come to do
what you want,
as the Scriptures say.”
8The Law teaches that offerings and sacrifices must be made because of sin. But why did Christ mention these things and say that God did not want them? 9Well, it was to do away with offerings and sacrifices and to replace them. This is what he meant by saying to God, “I have come to do what you want.” 10So we are made holy because Christ obeyed God and offered himself once for all.
11 The priests do their work each day, and they keep on offering sacrifices that can never take away sins. 12 But Christ offered himself as a sacrifice that is good forever. Now he is sitting at God's right side, 13and he will stay there until his enemies are put under his power. 14By his one sacrifice he has forever set free from sin the people he brings to God.
15The Holy Spirit also speaks of this by telling us that the Lord said,
16 “When the time comes,
I will make an agreement
with them.
I will write my laws
on their minds and hearts.
17 Then I will forget
about their sins
and no longer remember
their evil deeds.”
18When sins are forgiven, there is no more need to offer sacrifices.
Encouragement and Warning
19My friends, the blood of Jesus gives us courage to enter the most holy place 20by a new way that leads to life! And this way takes us through the curtain that is Christ himself.
21We have a great high priest who is in charge of God's house. 22 So let's come near God with pure hearts and a confidence that comes from having faith. Let's keep our hearts pure, our consciences free from evil, and our bodies washed with clean water. 23We must hold tightly to the hope we say is ours. After all, we can trust the one who made the agreement with us. 24We should keep on encouraging each other to be thoughtful and to do helpful things. 25Some people have given up the habit of meeting for worship, but we must not do that. We should keep on encouraging each other, especially since you know that the day of the Lord's coming is getting closer.
26No sacrifices can be made for people who decide to sin after they find out about the truth. 27 They are God's enemies, and all they can look forward to is a terrible judgment and a furious fire. 28 If two or more witnesses accused someone of breaking the Law of Moses, that person could be put to death. 29 But it is much worse to dishonor God's Son and to disgrace the blood of the promise that made us holy. And it is just as bad to insult the Holy Spirit, who shows us mercy. 30 We know that God has said he will punish and take revenge. We also know that the Scriptures say the Lord will judge his people. 31It is a terrible thing to fall into the hands of the living God!
32Don't forget all the hard times you went through when you first received the light. 33Sometimes you were abused and mistreated in public, and at other times you shared in the sufferings of others. 34You were kind to people in jail. And you gladly let your possessions be taken away, because you knew you had something better, something that would last forever.
35Keep on being brave! It will bring you great rewards. 36Learn to be patient, so you will please God and be given what he has promised. 37 As the Scriptures say,
“God is coming soon!
It won't be very long.
38The people God accepts
will live because
of their faith.
But he isn't pleased
with anyone
who turns back.”
39We are not like those people who turn back and get destroyed. We will keep on having faith until we are saved.
translation_text:
Kiresta kaabɛ la buyina za'a za'a
1Bala, ze'elego la en yeen dɛna yinyiligo bo' yelesuma la en kini na la, gee dagi yelesuma la yelemɛŋerɛ naanɛ n bala la, kaabegɔ yiŋɔ la en kaaberi yuunɛ woo kan ta'am bahɛ ti sɛba en dole ku la dɛna nɛreba en bi'ɛ kahegɛ. 2Han dagi ni bala, ba kan bahɛ ni ba kaabegɔ, sɛba en na'aheri ku la, han duuhe ba mɛhi buyina za'a za'a, ka le tari ni be'em puti'ira? 3Gee, kaabegɔ kuna puan, la tiiheri la be'em yele, yuunɛ en kaara yuunɛ. 4Se'ere en sɔi la, la kan ta'am iŋɛ ti lɔlehi la buuhi ziim ta'am saalum be'em. 5 Lan vuti fifihe ti Kiresta ta wa'am timpaberɛ wa zuo na la, a yeti,
“Kaabegɔ, la bo'olum fum ka boti,
gee iŋa ti fum maahum bo' mam.
6Nyɔ'a bo'olum, la be'em kaabegɔ bo'olum,
fum suure ka boti ba.
7Bala ti mam yeti, Yinɛ bihɛ, mam wa'am na ti n tum la fum sumboolum Oo Yinɛ,
(wuu gɔŋɔ la puan, n gulehɛ mam yele se'em la).”
8En yele se'em zuin wa yeti, “Fum suure bii fum nini tika ka boi kaabegɔ, la bo'olum bii nyɔ'a bo'olum la be'em duuhego bo'olum puan la” (ba bo'ori bana woo dɔla la nɔze'elego la), 9gee nyaa pa'ahɛ yeti, “Bihɛ, mam wa'am na ti n tum la fum sumboolum.” Bala, a saalum yia nɔpu'ulegɔ la bahɛ mɛ, ti a ta'am sɛ yi'i nɔpu'ulegɔ la. 10Ti la dɛna la Yinɛ mɛŋa sumboolum zuo, ti ba pee tumam doohe Yezu Kiresta inganɛ la en dikɛ kaabɛ buyina za'a za'a bo' nɛra woo la.
11 Gee malema daana woo ze' mɛ beere en yilegeri beere a tumam la puan, kaabera kaabegɔ yiŋɔ mɛa tulena, kaabegɔ yiŋɔ mɛa en kan malum pee be'em bahɛ la. 12 Gee Kiresta kaabɛ la buyina bo' saŋa woo, kaabegɔ kuyina ma'a la bo' be'em ba'ahɛ la, a nyaa zi'ire la Yinɛ zuɔ nu'o, 13pɔhɛ bala ma'a ha, “a guri mɛ sansɛka ti a dinduma wan lebege a nama dafeere.” 14Se'ere en sɔi la, kaabegɔ kuyina ma'a puan, ti a bahɛ ti ba bi'ɛ kahegɛ saŋa woo, bamam sɛba en kɔ'ɔm dɛna filam la. 15Fa'a Sia la dela aze'nyɛdaana bo' dina wa, en yele tu yeti,
16 “Nɔpu'ulegɔ kuna ti n wan pu'ulɛ la ba,
dabeha aŋa la han ta tole. Daana la n yele.
N wan dikɛ n nɔze'elego iŋɛ ba suyan,
gee gulehɛ a iŋɛ ba puti'ira puan,”
17 a me pa'ahɛ yeti,
“N kan tɛra ba be'em, la ba ka fabele se'ere tuuma la le yɛ'ɛha.”
18Zi'an ti sugeri dia bɔna bo' yele ana, be'em duuhego kaabegɔ ka le bɔna.
Ŋmibega yi'a
19Bala zuo n suurɔ, tumam n diŋɛ tari puti'irɛ ti tu wan kɛ̃ Fa'a saraa la puan Yezu ziim la zuo la, 20doohe la sadɔɔ paalega vua la ti a yu'ɛ bo' tu, doohe la en ahegɛ tanɛ se'ere n beŋe la bahɛ la, (a iŋa en bala), 21la tumam en tari malema kiima kãtɛ Yinɛ yire la puan la, 22 bahɛ ya ti tu vurege du' la yelemɛŋerɛ suure, tari puti'irɛ n pirɛ la sakerɛ, ti tu suya miihi ti ba duuhe a be'em puti'irɛ, ti tu ihe pee la tuulum ko'om. 23Bahɛ ya ti tu gurɛ suŋa suŋa tu beere puti'irɛ sakerɛ yelehum la gee da miina, se'ere en sɔi la se'em daana en biŋe nuurɛ la dela yelemɛŋerɛ daana. 24Gee bahɛ ya ti tu biha tumam n wan iŋɛ se'em pagera taaba la nɔŋerɛ la itesuŋɔ, 25da zagehera ya lagena taaba, wuu basɛba itegɔ en de se'em la, gee ya kpɛmeha taaba, malum ita de gana bala, wuu yan nyɛ ti dabeherɛ la pɔri la.
26Gee tu han kɔ'ɔm mina gee bɔna be'em puan tumam en to'e yelemɛŋerɛ mi'ilum la ba'ahɛ la, kaabegɔ ka le yee wan kaabɛ bo' tu be'em, 27gee sɛla en wan wa'am na dela dabeem gakerɛ, la sunsunyiim bugum la en wan di dinduma la. 28Se'em woo en tuue Moose pa'alegɔ la, kiiri mɛ ti nimbu'ɔ ka bɔna, “Aze'nyɛ duma bayi' batã han diŋɛ tɔgɛ.” 29 Bala, namehɛ kãtɛ deni taaba ti yamam ti'iha ti ba en wan dikɛ bo' sɛba en ka dikɛ Yinɛ Dayua la yi' sɛla, tuura nɔpu'ulegɔ ziim la n dikɛ pee ba la, gee nyiiha zu'uhegɔ Sia la? 30 Se'ere en sɔi la, tu mi se'em Daana en yeti, “Leregere dela mam dinɛ, N wan lebehe yɔ la.” Gee le yeti,“Daana la wan gakɛ a nɛreba” la. 31La dela dabeem yele ti fum lu Yinɛ vua wa nu'uhen.
32Gee tiihɛ dabeha aŋa ha la, yan daa nyɛ niihum la, ya daa ŋmiberi mɛ la zika kãtɛ namehegɔ puan, 33saŋa se'ehi ba ni ba' diihe ya la vi nɛreba nɛŋan, la mɛlehegɔ, ti sahi se'ehi, ya naaɛ la sɛba ti ba ba' mɛleha. 34Se'ere en sɔi la, ya tari nimbu'ɔ mɛ bɔ'ɔra sɛba en boi paka deto puan, gee sakɛ la nyɛɛma ba han fãara ya lɔgerɔ, gee mina ti yamam mɛhi tari la sɛla en ani suŋa gee bɔna wuuha gana bala. 35Bala zuo, da bahɛ ya puti'irɛ dinɛ taaba, de tari la yɔɔrɛ kãtɛ kina na. 36Bala zuo, ya boti la ŋmibega, ti ya han ta tum Yinɛ sumboolum la ba'ahɛ, ya wan to'e nɔbiŋere la.
37 Gee la kelum wan, “iŋɛ fii wa,
ti se'em daana en ye' na la wan sirum wa'am na, gee kan gu'um;
38Gee mam tuuntɔɔ daana wa wan vɔna mɛ la sakerɛ.
Mam sia ka nyɛɛni la se'em en lebere pooren.”
39Gee tumam ka pa'ahɛ sɛba en lebere pooren, ni ta bɔregɛ la, gee sɛba en tari sakerɛ, bala zuo nyɛ faarɛ la puan.

english_text:
The Great Faith of God's People
1Faith makes us sure of what we hope for and gives us proof of what we cannot see. 2 It was their faith that made our ancestors pleasing to God.
3 Because of our faith, we know that the world was made at God's command. We also know that what can be seen was made out of what cannot be seen.
4 Because Abel had faith, he offered God a better sacrifice than Cain did. God was pleased with him and his gift, and even though Abel is now dead, his faith still speaks for him.
5 Enoch had faith and did not die. He pleased God, and God took him up to heaven. This is why his body was never found. 6But without faith no one can please God. We must believe that God is real and rewards everyone who searches for him.
7 Because Noah had faith, he was warned about something that had not yet happened. He obeyed and built a boat that saved him and his family. In this way the people of the world were judged, and Noah was given the blessings that come to everyone who pleases God.
8 Abraham had faith and obeyed God. He was told to go to the land that God had said would be his, and he left for a country he had never seen. 9 Because Abraham had faith, he lived as a stranger in the promised land. He lived there in a tent, and so did Isaac and Jacob, who were later given the same promise. 10Abraham did this, because he was waiting for the eternal city God had planned and built.
11 Even when Sarah was too old to have children, she had faith that God would do what he had promised, and she had a son. 12 Her husband Abraham was almost dead, but he became the ancestor of many people. In fact, there are as many of them as there are stars in the sky or grains of sand along the seashore.
13 Every one of those people died. But they still had faith, even though they had not received what they had been promised. They were glad just to see these things from far away, and they agreed that they were only strangers and foreigners on this earth. 14When people talk this way, it is clear they are looking for a place to call their own. 15If they had been talking about the land where they had once lived, they could have gone back at any time. 16But they were looking forward to a better home in heaven. This is why God wasn't ashamed for them to call him their God. He even built a city for them.
17-18 Abraham had been promised that Isaac, his only son, would continue his family. But when Abraham was tested, he had faith and was willing to sacrifice Isaac, 19because he was sure that God could raise people to life. This was just like getting Isaac back from death.
20 Isaac had faith, and he promised blessings to Jacob and Esau. 21 Later, when Jacob was about to die, he leaned on his walking stick and worshiped. Then because of his faith he blessed each of Joseph's sons. 22 And right before Joseph died, he had faith that God would lead the people of Israel out of Egypt. So he told them to take his bones with them.
23 Because Moses' parents had faith, they kept him hidden until he was three months old. They saw that he was a beautiful child, and they were not afraid to disobey the king's orders. 24 Then after Moses grew up, his faith made him refuse to be called the king's grandson. 25 He chose to be mistreated with God's people instead of having the good time that sin could bring for a little while. 26Moses knew that the treasures of Egypt were not as wonderful as what he would receive from suffering for the Messiah, and he looked forward to his reward.
27Because of his faith, Moses left Egypt. Moses had seen the invisible God and wasn't afraid of the king's anger. 28 His faith also made him celebrate Passover. He sprinkled the blood of animals on the doorposts, so that the first-born sons of the people of Israel would not be killed by the destroying angel.
29 Because of their faith, the people walked through the Red Sea on dry land. But when the Egyptians tried to do it, they were drowned.
30 God's people had faith, and when they had walked around the city of Jericho for seven days, its walls fell down.
31 Rahab had been a prostitute, but she had faith and welcomed the spies. So she wasn't killed with the people who disobeyed.
32 What else can I say? There isn't enough time to tell about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the prophets. 33 Their faith helped them conquer kingdoms, and because they did right, God made promises to them. They closed the jaws of lions 34 and put out raging fires and escaped from the swords of their enemies. Although they were weak, they were given the strength and power to chase foreign armies away.
35 Some women received their loved ones back from death. Many of these people were tortured, but they refused to be released. They were sure they would get a better reward when the dead are raised to life. 36 Others were made fun of and beaten with whips, and some were chained in jail. 37 Still others were stoned to death or sawed in two or killed with swords. Some had nothing but sheep skins or goat skins to wear. They were poor, mistreated, and tortured. 38The world did not deserve these good people, who had to wander in deserts and on mountains and had to live in caves and holes in the ground.
39All of them pleased God because of their faith! But still they died without being given what had been promised. 40This was because God had something better in store for us. And he did not want them to reach the goal of their faith without us.
translation_text:
Sakerɛ vuurɛ
1Nananawa, sakerɛ dela suure en ku gura beere puti'irɛ, suure en kɔ'ɛ gura sɛla ti nini ka nyɛ. 2Yelemɛŋerɛ, sakerɛ zuo, ti nɛreba yuum tɔgera ba yele. 3 Sakerɛ zuo ti tu bɔkɛ ti Yinɛ naam saazuo la timpaberɛ wa mɛ la a yelehum ma'a, bala, sɛla ti tu nyɛta wa ze'ele la sɛla ti tu ka nyɛta puan na.
Abɛl, Enɔki la Nowa makerɛ
4 Sakerɛ zuo ti Abɛl bo' Yinɛ bo'olum sebo en tigɛ nini gana Keen bo'olum la. Doohe ŋwana zuo, ti ba tɔgera a yele ti a dela tuuntɔɔ nɛra. Yinɛ mɛŋa en de aze'nyɛ daana bo' a bo'olum la. La en pun ki la, gee la bala za'a, a sakerɛ la zuo, a kelum tɔgera mɛ. 5Sakerɛ zuo ti Yinɛ tee Enɔki kiŋɛ ti a ka makɛ lem kum. “Ba yuum ka nyɛ en se'ere en sɔi la, Yinɛ en dikɛ en kiŋɛ.” Gee ti teere wa wa'am na la, ba pun tɔgɛ a yele mɛ ti, “a tigɛ la Yinɛ nini.” 6Bala, sakerɛ han ka bɔna, la kpe'em mɛ ti fum tigɛ Yinɛ nini, se'ere en sɔi la, se'em woo en wa'am a zi'an na, dela a mina ti Yinɛ boi mɛ, gee yɔɔra sɛba woo en eere en la ninmu'urɛ. 7 Sakerɛ zuo ti Nowa, Yinɛ kagɛ en doohe yele sɛ'a en wan wa'am na, ti Nowa nam yetɔgum la ninmu'urɛ, gee kpa' daka kãtɛ la ti a faaɛ a yire. Yele dina ti Nowa yuum dikɛ gakɛ timpaberɛ wa, gee nyaa sooe vaaɛ tuntɔɔnɛ en dole sakerɛ puan la.
Aberaham sakerɛ
8 Sakerɛ zuo ti Aberaham nam en yuum yi' en ti a nɔgɛ kiŋɛ zi'an ti a wan ta sooe ti ka dɛna a sɔ'ɔlum la. A yuum sirum ihege yɛ'a mɛ, gee ka mina en ye' zi'an la. 9 Sakerɛ zuo ti Aberaham ta zi'ire saŋa fii wa, tinsɛka puan ti Yinɛ biŋe nuurɛ ti a wan dikɛ bo' en la, wuu en de saana ka puan la, a ki'ire la suga puan, bala mɛa ti Aziki la Yakɔbe me iŋɛ, bamam sɛba la eŋa en lagum vaaɛ nɔbiŋere sɔ'ɔlum bumɔ mɛa la. 10Se'ere en sɔi la, Aberaham yuum guri la tinkãtɛ en tari ɛ̃berɛ, ti ka gula, la ka mɛta dɛna Yinɛ. 11 Sakerɛ zuo ti a to'e dɔgum paŋa nɔbiŋere, la en daa pun ba' kuregɛ la, ti Saara me ka dɔgera la, beni zuo, a yuum nam mɛ ti se'em en biŋe nuurɛ la dela yelemɛŋerɛ daana. 12 Bala, ze'ele nɛra ayima wa puan na, nɛre se'em en ani wuu a ki mɛ la puan na, ti yaahi wa'am na, “zo'e wuu ŋmarebibehi en zo'e se'em sagbama zuo ha la, zo'e kan ta'am kãalɛ wuu kulaa tintombi'ihego la.”
13 Bana woo wa'am na ki mɛ la ba sakerɛ la, gee ka to'e Yinɛ en biŋe nuurɛ ti a bo' ba sɛla la, gee ba nyɛ la mɛ ba suyan zaaɛ zaarɛ ha ti la kini na, ti ba to'e la. Ba daa yeti bamam dela saama, dɛna ɛɛreba timpaberɛ wa zuo. 14Nɛresɛba en tɔgeri ŋwana la, la niiɛ mɛ ti ba eere la ba mɛŋa tiŋa ti ba zi'ire. 15Yelemɛŋerɛ ba han ti'ihɛ ni la ba tiŋa ti ba bahɛ pooren ha la yele, ba tari ni sore ti ba lebe. 16Gee nananawa lan de se'em la dela, ba suure kɛ̃ mɛ la tinsɛka en gani bala, tinsɛka en ze'eti saazuo na la. Bala zuo, Yinɛ ka tari vi la ba yi'ira en ba Yinɛ. Yelemɛŋerɛ, a sirum maahum la tiŋa biŋe ba.
17 Sakerɛ zuo, ti Aberaham, Yinɛ wa makɛ en, ti a dikɛ Aziki kaabɛ. Eŋa se'em en to'e a nɔbiŋere lɔkɔ la, yuum maahum mɛ ti a dikɛ a dayɔba'arɛ wa kaabɛ. 18 A dayɔsɛka ti Yinɛ yele en yeti, “Aziki puan ti fum wan nyɛ yaahi ti ba dikɛ sigɛ hɔ la.” 19Aberaham yuum ti'ihɛ nyɛ ti la de sira, ti Yinɛ wan ta'am ihege nɛra kum puan lebena, tɔgɛ biŋere puan a yuum sirum lebe to'e en mɛ. 20Sakerɛ zuo ti Aziki ka' sum bahɛ Yakɔbe la Esɔ beere puan. 21Sakerɛ zuo ti Yakɔbe en wa pɔra kum la, a ka' sum bahɛ Yosefe dayɔɔhi zuo, “Nyiga a doore zuo na'ahera.” 22 Sakerɛ zuo ti Yosefe ta pɔra kum gee tɔgɛ bo' Iziraleduma, ba yɛhega yele, gee pa'alɛ ban wan pi' en se'em.
Moose sakerɛ
23 Sakerɛ zuo ti Moose dɔgereba yuum sugɛ en ban yuum dɔgɛ en ti a ta paaɛ ŋmarehi sitã la. Se'ere en sɔi la, ba yuum nyɛ ti bia la sum mɛ, ti dabeem ka tara ba la naba la nuurɛ la ti a bo' la. 24 Sakerɛ zuo ti Moose en yuum ta zo'e la, a zagehɛ ti, ba da yi'ira eŋa Faro poyua bia, 25gee tugum looe ti a nameha la Yinɛ nɛreba la nyana a dita nyɛlum be'em puan dabeha fii wa. 26A yuum nam ya ti Kiresta zuo a wan to'e kɛhega la namehegɔ, ti la dɛna tarega kãtɛ bo' en, nyana Igipiti tarega la, se'ere en sɔi la, a yuum biheri la yɔɔri kãtɛ la en boi nɛŋa ha la. 27Sakerɛ zuo ti a bahɛ Igipiti, ka zɔta dabeem la naba la sunsunyiim la. A yuum kɔ'ɔm ŋmibera mɛ kina wuu a nyɛ la se'em daana ti ba ka nyɛta la. 28 Sakerɛ zuo ti a doohe azɔɛtole malema la, la ziim miihego, ti Sagena la en dole kuura bikiinduma la da ta'am kalum Izirale bikiima.
Izirale sakerɛ puan gendɔɔrɔ
29 Sakerɛ zuo ti nɛreba la daa sige mɔgemɔlegɔ la puan kiŋɛ yakɛ wuu la dela kɛ'ɛŋa la, gee Igipitiduma la en se'em ti ba me iŋɛ bala la, ba yee la ko'om la puan. 30 Sakerɛ zuo ti Yeriko nangɔɔma la lu, Izirale nɛreba la en kaari dɛ muna ta paaɛ dabeha ayopɔi daarɛ la. 31 Sakerɛ zuo ti Arahab en de yalema yuum ka lagum nyɛ sageŋɔ la sɛba woo en yuum ka nam la, se'ere en sɔi la, a yuum to'e Izirale viihereba la mɛ la suma'ahum.
32 Beni ti n wan le yele pa'ahɛ? Saŋa kan bɔna bo' mam ti n yele Gidiyɔn, Barake, Samsin Yɛfita, Deviti la Samuwɛle, la nɔtɔgeheba la, 33 sɛba en yuum ze'ele sakerɛ puan nyaŋɛ tinkãra, gakɛ la yelemɛŋerɛ, ze'ele to'e sɛla ti Yinɛ biŋe nuurɛ la, mum gbigema nɔya, 34 kiihe bugum en taaɛ dita ka tara makerɛ, piiɛ kuura sɔ'a nuuren, nyɛ paŋa tɔregɔ puan lebege kansanhi pɛntɛrɛ puan, bahɛ ti pɛntiireba en de saama zɔ zɔpɛɛlega. 35 Ti pɔgehi nɛreba en tabelɛ ki, le ihege ti ba to'ohe ba. Ba mɛlehɛ basɛba mɛ, gee ti ba zagehɛ ti bamam kan yehe paka deo la puan, ti ba to'e ihegere sunɛ se'ere n gani bala. 36 Basɛba to'ohe la kɛhega la ŋmɛ'kãtɛ, pun ta paaɛ kuto zɔtɔ ba'a, la paka deto puan. 37 Ba lobe basɛba mɛ la kuga ku, aahum basɛba wele wele, kɔrum basɛba la sɔ'ɔhi. Ba yɛ la piihi la buuhi gana ɛɛra la nimbu'ɔ, kua, la mɛlehegɔ, 38ba eere nyaara la kpaahenɛ zi'ihi, zɔya zuto, tahi leŋen, tiŋan yogero puan. Tiŋa wa ka ana suŋa bo' ba.
39Gee yele ana za'a la, la ban pun pɛgɛ ba la ba sakerɛ la, ba ka nyaŋɛ to'e sɛla ti Yinɛ biŋe nuurɛ ti a bo' la, 40se'ere en sɔi la, Yinɛ maahum la sɛla en gani bala biŋe, ti tumam la bamam lagum taaba bi'ɛ kahegɛ.

english_text:
A Large Crowd of Witnesses
1 Such a large crowd of witnesses is all around us! So we must get rid of everything that slows us down, especially the sin that just won't let go. And we must be determined to run the race that is ahead of us. 2 We must keep our eyes on Jesus, who leads us and makes our faith complete. He endured the shame of being nailed to a cross, because he knew later on he would be glad he did. Now he is seated at the right side of God's throne! 3So keep your mind on Jesus, who put up with many insults from sinners. Then you won't get discouraged and give up.
4None of you have yet been hurt in your battle against sin. 5 But you have forgotten that the Scriptures say to God's children,
“When the Lord punishes you,
don't make light of it,
and when he corrects you,
don't be discouraged.
6The Lord corrects the people
he loves
and disciplines those
he calls his own.”
7Be patient when you are being corrected! This is how God treats his children. Don't all parents correct their children? 8God corrects all his children, and if he doesn't correct you, then you don't really belong to him. 9Our earthly fathers correct us, and we still respect them. Isn't it even better to be given true life by letting our spiritual Father correct us?
10Our human fathers correct us for a short time, and they do it as they think best. But God corrects us for our own good, because he wants us to be holy, as he is. 11It is never fun to be corrected. In fact, at the time it is always painful. But if we learn to obey by being corrected, we will do right and live at peace.
12 Now stand up straight! Stop your knees from shaking 13 and walk a straight path. Then lame people will be healed, instead of getting worse.
Warning against Turning from God
14Try to live at peace with everyone! Live a clean life. If you don't, you will never see the Lord. 15 Make sure no one misses out on God's wonderful kindness. Don't let anyone become bitter and cause trouble for the rest of you. 16 Watch out for immoral and ungodly people like Esau, who sold his future blessing for only one meal. 17 You know how he later wanted it back. But there was nothing he could do to change things, even though he begged his father and cried.
18 You have not come to a place like Mount Sinai that can be seen and touched. There is no flaming fire or dark cloud or storm 19or trumpet sound. The people of Israel heard a voice speak. But they begged it to stop, 20 because they could not obey its commands. They were even told to kill any animal that touched the mountain. 21The sight was so frightening that Moses said he shook with fear.
22You have now come to Mount Zion and to the heavenly Jerusalem. This is the city of the living God, where thousands and thousands of angels have come to celebrate. 23Here you will find all of God's dearest children, whose names are written in heaven. And you will find God himself, who judges everyone. Here also are the spirits of those good people who have been made perfect. 24 And Jesus is here! He is the one who makes God's new agreement with us, and his sprinkled blood says much better things than the blood of Abel.
25 Make sure you obey the one who speaks to you. The people did not escape, when they refused to obey the one who spoke to them at Mount Sinai. Do you think you can possibly escape, if you refuse to obey the one who speaks to you from heaven? 26 When God spoke the first time, his voice shook only the earth. This time he has promised to shake the earth once again, and heaven too.
27The words “once again” mean that these created things will someday be shaken and removed. Then what cannot be shaken will last. 28We should be grateful we were given a kingdom that cannot be shaken. And in this kingdom we please God by worshiping him and by showing him great honor and respect. 29 Our God is like a destructive fire!
translation_text:
Yezu itegɔ
1Bala, aze'nyɛ wa en zo'e se'em wuu sagbanɛ wa kaaɛ tu mum wa zuo, bahɛ ya ti tu dikɛ tibehegɔ seko woo, la be'em sebo woo en ba' tabera, gee ana la tɔ kankaŋi la biŋe kinkɛleŋa, gee bahɛ ya ti tu zɔta la ŋmibega, zɔ sɛka en gã' tu nɛŋan wa. 2Tu biha suŋa suŋa Yezu en de sakerɛ nɛŋa daana, se'em daana n de sakerɛ la ba'ahegɔ daana la. Se'em ti nyɛɛma sɛ'a en dikɛ biŋe en la zuo, a daa ŋmibe mɛ ta paaɛ pumpuuredɔɔ la zuo, ka fabela dɔɔ zuo kum la nyanɛ la, nyaa wa'am na zi'a a zi'a zi'an Yinɛ na'am kuka la zuo, zuɔ nu'o.
3Ti'ihɛ ya bihɛ Yezu en daa ŋmibe se'em namehegɔ seko taaba ti be'em duma daa dikɛ namehɛ en la, bala ti yamam me kan taregera bii ya suure sagum. 4Yan zigeri la be'em la, ya nan ka zigɛ paaɛ ze'sɛka en de ya ziim ka'ɛ. 5 Ya me pun tamɛ kpemehego seko en gulehɛ pa'alɛ ti ya dela Yinɛ kɔma la. La yeti,
“N bia, da bihɛ Daana tube-dɔlegerɛ la yoo,
bii fum suure sagum, a han dɔlegɛ fum tuberɛ.
6Se'ere en sɔi la, Daana la nameheri la sɛba ti a nɔŋɛ,
gee dɔlegera bisɛka woo ti a to'e.”
7Ya ha ŋmibera makerɛ puan tube-dɔlegerɛ zuo. Yinɛ iti ya mɛ wuu a kɔma la. Bikani en boi ti ka dɔgera ka dɔlegera ka tuberɛ? 8Ya han ka to'e tube-dɔlegerɛ se'ere ti kɔma woo tɔ'ɔha la, ya dela kɔm-yooro, gee dagi Yinɛ kɔma. 9Le yɛ'ɛha, tu tari tu dɔgereba mɛ, ti ba dɔlegera tu tuba, gee ti tu nana ba. La tugum dagena tu malum bɔta ti tu dikɛ tu mɛhi iŋɛ Sɔ sɛka en sɔi sɛɛhi la nu'uhen la tu vɔna? 10Tu dɔgereba ni dɔlegɛ tu tuba la saŋa fii wa wuu bamam en bihɛ ti la nari se'em la, gee Yinɛ dɔlegeri tu tuba la tumam mɛhi sum zuo, ti la bahɛ ti tu ta lagum tara a tuulum la. 11Tube dɔlegerɛ woo tɔi mɛ, gee la nyani nyɛlum en wan bɔna saŋa fii wa. Ba'ahegɔ za'a, tube-dɔlegerɛ la ni tari la suma'ahum wala sɛ'a en de tuuntɔɔ vom bɔ'ɔra sɛba ti tube-dɔlegerɛ bi'ihɛ ba la.
12 Bala, zɛkɛ ya nu'uhi wa en ki yula wa, kpemehe ya duma wa en tɛteni wa, 13 maalɛ fum sore la suŋa bo' fum nama, ti sɛla en de wobete da sugehe, gee a tugum naaɛ taaba.
Da zagehɛ ya Yinɛ zu'uhegɔ la
14Eere ya suma'ahum ninmu'urɛ nɛra woo, la fa'a vom sebo en han ka bɔna, nɛra kan ta'am nyɛ Daana la. 15 Bihɛ ya suŋa, ti ya se'em da koŋe Yinɛ zu'uhegɔ la. Da bahɛ ya ti too nyɛgerɛ yehe ya puan na, tari daaŋɔ wa'am na, ti ya doohe de puan galum nɛreba zo'e zo'e. 16 Bihɛ ya mɛhi suŋa suŋa ti ya se'em da ana wuu Esɔ, se'em en ka ta' a mɛŋa, ka zɔta Yinɛ la, se'em en yuum koohe a kinɔ dia buyina ma'a zuo la. 17 Ya mi' ti pooren, en yuum ta bɔta ti a sooevaaɛ ka'am a sɔ zi'an la, a sɔ la yuum zagehɛ en mɛ se'ere en sɔi la, sore yuum ka boi pika pika bo' en ti a wan ta'am tee yele la, la en yuum pun ɛɛra a ka'am la la nintam la. 18Ya nan ka paaɛ zi'an ti ya wan ta'am kalum la na, bugum peelum la puan, la lika gbareti la zi'an na, la ze'sɛka en gbiregeri la, 19la tintanɛ peebego la, la kua sɛka tugum ti ka kɛleheba bɛlena ti ka pun da le tɔgɛ yele yinɛ pa'ahɛ la. 20 (Se'ere en sɔi la ba kan nyaŋɛ tara en bo' a nuurɛ la se'em la, ti “Duŋa han pun kalum zoore la, ka dela ba lobe ka ku” la. 21 Yelemɛŋerɛ, zi'an la yuum ba' tara la dabeem gaŋɛ ti Moose yeti, “Mam gbi'iri mɛ la dabeem.”) 22Gee yamam paaɛ la zoore se'ere yu'urɛ en yi'iri Zaayɔn la puan na, tinsɛka en de Yinɛ vua wa tiŋa la puan, tinsɛka en de Yerusalɛm sɛka en boi saazuo ha la, ya paaɛ la suŋereba en zo'e kan ta'am kãalɛ la lageŋɔ kãtɛ en boi kuyima, 23ya wa'am la lageŋɔ seko en de kɔmdiina sɛba yu'ura en gulehɛ bɔna tinsuŋan puan la na, ya wa'am la Yinɛ se'ere en de sɛla woo gakera la zi'an na, Ya wa'am la tuuntɔɔ duma sɛɛhi la n bi'ɛ kahegɛ la zi'an na. 24 Ya wa'am la Yezu en de nupu'ŋmɛ'ɛra nɔpu'ule paalega la puan la zi'an na, la ziim sebo en dikɛ miihi, gee tɔgera yelesuma gana Abɛl ziim la zi'an na.
25 Bihɛ ya suŋa la ya da zagehɛ se'em en kageri ya wa. Nɛreba daa han ka piiɛ ban da zagehɛ se'em en daa kagɛ ba tiŋa wa zuo la, tumam yeti tu iŋɛ la ŋwani piiɛ la fii me, tu ha zagehɛ se'em en kageri tɔ saazuo na wa. 26 Sankaŋa ha la, a kua ma'a en yuum miim timpaberɛ wa, gee nananawa, a biŋe la nuurɛ ti “Le yɛ'ɛha, n wan le miim, gee dagi timpaberɛ wa ma'a, gee la saazuo za'a.” 27Yetɔge buna wa “Le yɛ'ɛha wa,” pa'ali ti, a yeti a vuɛ la sɛla en miini la bahɛ bana dela naaŋɔ lɔgerɔ n bala, ti sɛla woo n ka miini la yee. 28Bala zuo, tumam en yeti tu to'e sɔ'ɔlum sebo en ka miini la zuo, bahɛ ya ti tu bo' ya Yinɛ fara, doohe la na'ahegɔ kaabegɔ seko taaba en tigɛ nini, ti duma kpa'a, la dabeem bɔna bini. 29 Yelemɛŋerɛ, tu Yinɛ la dela bugum sebo en diti kãbera.

english_text:
Service That Pleases God
1Keep being concerned about each other as the Lord's followers should.
2 Be sure to welcome strangers into your home. By doing this, some people have welcomed angels as guests, without even knowing it.
3Remember the Lord's people who are in jail and be concerned for them. Don't forget those who are suffering, but imagine you are there with them.
4 Have respect for marriage. Always be faithful to your partner, because God will punish anyone who is immoral or unfaithful in marriage.
5 Don't fall in love with money. Be satisfied with what you have. The Lord has promised that he will not leave us or desert us. 6 This should make you feel like saying,
“The Lord helps me!
Why should I be afraid
of what people
can do to me?”
7Don't forget about your leaders who taught you God's message. Remember what kind of lives they lived and try to have faith like theirs.
8Jesus Christ never changes! He is the same yesterday, today, and forever. 9Don't be fooled by any kind of strange teachings. It is better to receive strength from God's gift of undeserved grace than to depend on certain foods. After all, these foods don't really help the people who eat them. 10But we have an altar where even the priests who serve in the place of worship have no right to eat.
11 After the high priest offers the blood of animals as a sin offering, the bodies of those animals are burned outside the camp. 12Jesus himself suffered outside the city gate, so his blood would make people holy. 13This is why we should go outside the camp to Jesus and share in his disgrace. 14On this earth we don't have a city that lasts forever, but we are waiting for such a city.
15Our sacrifice is to keep offering praise to God in the name of Jesus. 16But don't forget to help others and to share your possessions with them. This too is like offering a sacrifice that pleases God.
17Obey your leaders and do what they say. They are watching over you, and they must answer to God. So don't make them sad as they do their work. Make them happy. Otherwise, they won't be able to help you at all.
18Pray for us. Our consciences are clear, and we always try to live right. 19I especially want you to pray that I can visit you again soon.
Final Prayers and Greetings
20God gives peace, and he raised our Lord Jesus Christ from death. Now Jesus is like a Great Shepherd whose blood was used to make God's eternal agreement with his flock. 21 I pray God will make you ready to obey him and that you will always be eager to do right. May Jesus help you do what pleases God. To Jesus Christ be glory forever and ever! Amen.
22My friends, I have written only a short letter to encourage you, and I beg you to pay close attention to what I have said.
23By now you surely must know that our friend Timothy is out of jail. If he gets here in time, I will bring him with me when I come to visit you.
24Please give my greetings to your leaders and to the rest of the Lord's people.
His followers from Italy send you their greetings.
25I pray that God will be kind to all of you!
translation_text:
Tuunsɛ'a en tigeri Yinɛ nini
1Bahɛ ya ti suuɔ nɔŋerɛ yee saŋa woo. 2 Da zagehɛ ya tɔ'ɔha saama, gee sɛba iŋɛ la bala ta to'ohe suŋereba gee ka baŋɛ. 3Tɛri ya sɛba en boi paka deen la yele, wuu ya lagum bɔna la paka deen la ba la, sɛba ti ba mɛleha ba la, wuu yamam mɛhi ti ba mɛleha la. 4Bahɛ ya ti pɔgedire la sire-ele tara na'ahegɔ ya za'a zi'an, ti pɔgedire la sire-ele suŋɔ la da galum, se'ere en sɔi la, Yinɛ wan gakɛ yaluntuuma duma, la kabohi duma mɛ. 5 Tari ya ya vom suŋa ti bu da kɛ̃ ligenɔŋerɛ puan, gee bahɛ ya ti ya nini tigɛ la sɛla ti ya tara. Se'ere en sɔi la, a yele tu yeti, “N kan malum bahɛ ya, bii n zagehɛ ya.” 6 Ŋwana zuo la, tu wan ta'am yele gee ti dabeem ka tara tɔ yeti,
“Daana la en de mam suŋera,
N kan zɔta dabeem.
Beni ti nɛra wan ta'am iŋɛ mam?”
7Tɛra ya nɛheduma, sɛba en tɔgɛ Yinɛ yelehum la bo' ya la. Bihɛ ya ban daa vɔi ba vom se'em, la ya tɔgehɛ ba sakerɛ la. 8Yezu Kiresta dela bala mɛa zaam, zina, la saŋa woo. 9Da bahɛ ya ti pa'ali yooro yima yima ziira ya kaara zi'an woo, se'ere en sɔi la, la ani suŋa ti zu'uhegɔ kpemehe suure la, nyana dia kihega yɛla, yele sɛ'a en ka suŋɛ sɛba en dole a la. 10Tumam tari la kaabegɔ bimbine se'ere ti sɛba en ze' tanɛ deo la puan kaabera la ka tari sore ti ba dita kaabegɔ dia la. 11 Se'ere en sɔi la, duhi se'ehi ziim ti malema kiima la tari kɛ̃ Fa'a saraa la puan ti bu dɛna be'em duuhego kaabegɔ la, ba ni nyɔ' si la tiiheŋɔ la yiŋa ha. 12Bala zuo ti Yezu namehɛ tiŋa la yiŋa ha, ti a pee nɛreba be'em la a mɛŋa ziim. 13Bahɛ ya ti tu kiŋɛ ya a zi'an tiiheŋɔ la yiŋa la ha, la tu ta lagum di nyanɛ se'ere ti a ŋmibe de puan la. 14Tiŋa wa zuo, tu ka tari tinsɛka n wan bɔna wuuha, gee tu biheri la tiŋa sɛka n ye' na la. 15Doohe eŋa puan, yi bahɛ ya ti daarɛ woo, tu bɔ'ɔra Yinɛ tu na'ahegɔ kaabegɔ en de tu nɔgbama wala ti tu puta a yu'urɛ la. 16Da zagehɛ ya ti ya tuna sum, gee tɔta yan tari sɛla la taaba, gee kaabegɔ kuna taaba en tigeri Yinɛ nini.
17Nane ya ya nɛhi duma, gee sigehe ya mɛhi bo' ba, gee bamam en biheri ya vom, gee wan ta yele ban tuni se'em. Bo' ya ba sore ti ba tuna ba tuuma la nyɛɛma gee dagi ba si'ina. La han ana bala, ya kan nyɛ nyuurɔ.
18Pu'uhi ya bɔ'ɔra tɔ, gee tumam mi' ti tumam tari la putɛ'sunɛ, ti tu suure bɔta ti tu tuna la yelemɛŋerɛ sɛla woo puan. 19N yeti ya mɛ la ninmu'urɛ, ti ya tuna ŋwana wa gana sɛla woo, ti n ta'am le lebe ya zi'an kalum na.
Pu'uhegɔ
20Nananawa, Yinɛ se'em en de suma'ahum daana la, se'em daana en tari a piihi dunkiin kãtɛ wa ze'ele kum puan lebe na la, tu Daana Yezu Kiresta doohe a ziim la nɔpu'ulegɔ la en ka tari ba'ahegɔ la puan, 21wan bahɛ ti ya bi'ɛ tunsunɛ woo puan, ti ya ta'am tum a sumboolum, doohe la en boi tu puan tuna la tɔ, tuunsɛ'a en tigeri a nini Yezu puan, se'em ti suŋa dɛna a dinɛ saŋa woo. Taari.
22N beleni ya mɛ n suurɔ, ŋmibe ya la n kpemehego yelehum wa, gee n yeen gulehɛ la girega girega bo' ya na. 23N boti ya mina ti ba bahɛ tu suuɔ Timoti, ti a han wa'am tɔtɔ na, a wan doohe la mam na ti n nyɛ ya. 24Pu'uhɛ ya nɛheduma, la nɛresunduma la woo bo' tu. Sɛba woo en boi Itali tiŋa pu'uheri ya na. 25Yinɛ zu'uhegɔ bɔna la ya za'a.

english_text:
1 From James, a servant of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Greetings to the twelve tribes scattered all over the world.
Faith and Wisdom
2 My friends, be glad, even if you have a lot of trouble. 3You know you learn to endure by having your faith tested. 4But you must learn to endure everything, so you will be completely mature and not lacking in anything.
5 If any of you need wisdom, you should ask God, and it will be given to you. God is generous and won't correct you for asking. 6But when you ask for something, you must have faith and not doubt. Anyone who doubts is like an ocean wave tossed around in a storm. 7-8If you are that kind of person, you can't make up your mind, and you surely can't be trusted. So don't expect the Lord to give you anything at all.
Poor People and Rich People
9Any of God's people who are poor should be glad he thinks so highly of them. 10 But any who are rich should be glad when God makes them humble. Rich people will disappear like wild flowers 11scorched by the burning heat of the sun. The flowers lose their blossoms, and their beauty is destroyed. This is how the rich will disappear, as they go about their business.
Trials and Temptations
12 God will bless you, if you don't give up when your faith is being tested. He will reward you with a glorious life, just as he rewards everyone who loves him.
13 Don't blame God when you are tempted! God cannot be tempted by evil, and he doesn't use evil to tempt others. 14We are tempted by our own desires that drag us off and trap us. 15Our desires make us sin, and when sin is finished with us, it leaves us dead.
16Don't be fooled, my dear friends. 17Every good and perfect gift comes down from the Father who created all the lights in the heavens. He is always the same and never makes dark shadows by changing. 18He wanted us to be his own special people, and so he sent the true message to give us new birth.
Hearing and Obeying
19 My dear friends, you should be quick to listen and slow to speak or to get angry. 20If you are angry, you cannot do any of the good things God wants done. 21You must stop doing anything immoral or evil. Instead be humble and accept the message planted in you to save you.
22Obey God's message! Don't fool yourselves by just listening to it. 23If you hear the message and don't obey it, you are like people who stare at themselves in a mirror 24and forget what they look like as soon as they leave. 25But you must never stop looking at the perfect law that sets you free. God will bless you in everything you do, if you listen and obey, and don't just hear and forget.
26If you think you are being religious, but can't control your tongue, you are fooling yourself, and your religion is useless. 27Religion that pleases God the Father must be pure and spotless. You must help needy orphans and widows and not let this world make you evil.
translation_text:
Pu'uhegɔ
1 Yemesi en de yameŋa bo' Yinɛ la Daana Yezu Kiresta la, en gulehɛ gɔŋɔ wa bɔ'ɔra yizuto pia la tuyi' la en nɔgɛ bɔna zi'an woo la.
Mam pu'uheri ya na.
Sakerɛ la Yɛm
2N suurɔ, ya han ni ta nyɛta maketooro seto woo, da dikɛ ya ku yi' sɛsɛla, gee tugum nyɛɛni ya. 3Se'ere en sɔi la, ya mi' ti ya sakerɛ makerɛ bo'ori ya la ŋmibega. 4Bahɛ ya ti ya ŋmibega la pirɛ, ti ya ta'am bi'ɛ kahegɛ ti sɛla da koŋe ya.
5Ya se'em han pɔ̃hegɛ yɛm, a suhɛ Yinɛ, se'em en bo'ori yabi yabi gee ka fabela la, gee a wan bo' fum. 6Gee suhɛ en la sakerɛ, gee da bu'ura. Se'ere en sɔi la, se'em n bu'uri ani wuu Ateko ko'mi'a ti kusebego tara ŋmɛ'ɛra kaara se'em la. 7Nɛre se'em en ani ŋwana da ti'iha ti a wan to'e sɛla Daana la zi'an. 8Se'ere en sɔi la nɛre-ina tari la puti'ira ayi' ayi', ka zɛ'ɛta se'ere puan.
Nɔŋɔ la Tarega
9Bahɛ ya ti suuɔ seko en sigehe ku mɛŋa la, ŋmɛ' a nyu'ɔ, la Yinɛ en zɛkɛ en la, 10 ti buntata me sigehe a mɛŋa, beni zuo, tarega wan mɛlum wuu mɔpuuro la. 11Se'ere en sɔi la, wuntɛɛŋa zoni mɛ na la tuulega, ku'ura vatɔ la, ti bu puuro woo luta, ti bu suŋa la Sagena. Bala mɛa ti buntateba wan ta bahɛ yoo ban mu'ɛ nini ba bumbɔrɛ la puan se'em la.
Magehegɔ la pã'ahegɔ
12Sum boi mɛ la se'em en ŋmiberi makerɛ puan. Ena daana nyaŋɛ magehegɔ la mɛ, wan to'e vom muŋa la, ti Daana la biŋe nuurɛ ti a bo' sɛba en nɔŋɛ en la. 13Se'em da bɔna ti makerɛ se'ere han paaɛ en, ti a yeti, “Yinɛ en makerɛ mam biha.” Se'ere en sɔi la, be'em kan ta'am makɛ Yinɛ bihɛ, Yinɛ mɛŋa me ka makerɛ se'em la be'em biha. 14Gee la han ta iŋɛ bala, nɛra mɛŋa kunkoma'ahum en ni pã'ahɛ en, ve'e en kɛ̃' makerɛ la puan. 15Ti kunkoma'ahum buna wa nyaa han ta nyɔkɛ puurɛ, bu dɔgeri la be'em, ti be'em buna wa han ta bi'ɛ kahegɛ, bu dɔgeri la kum. 16Da bahɛ ya ti se'em pã'ahɛ ya, n sunɔŋerɛ duma wa. 17Beni zuo, abo'yabiyabi woo, la bo'olum sumɔ woo ze'eti la saazuo, Sɔ la en de niihum daana la zi'an sigera na. Se'em puan ti ŋmɛlema la lika ka bɔna doohe teere se'ere puan. 18Doohe a mɛŋa puti'irɛ en de se'em la zuo, a dɔgɛ tu mɛ doohe a yelemɛŋerɛ yelehum la puan, ti tu dɛna wala diina a naaŋɔ la puan.
Kelehego la tuuma
19Ya dela ya bɔkɛ dina wa, n sunɔŋerɛ duma wa, bahɛ ya ti nɛra woo kɛleha kalam kalam, gee da tɔgera kalam kalam, bii ita suure kalam kalam. 20Se'ere en sɔi la, ya sunsunyiim la ka ŋwɔni Yinɛ tuuntɔɔ vom la. 21Dinɛ zuo, yehe ya mɛhi yaalegɔ woo puan, la tuunfi'iha kãra puan, gee sigehe ya mɛhi to'e yelehum la en burɛ ya puan tara paŋa wan ta'am faaɛ ya sɛɛhi bahɛ la.
22Gee me iti ya yelehum la en de se'em la, gee da yeen kelehe ya kelehego ma'a pã'ahɛ ya mɛhi. 23Se'ere en sɔi la, sɛba han yeen kɛleha yelehum la ma'a, gee ka tari bu tuna, ba ani mɛ wuu sɛba en ni bihɛ ba mɛhi biheŋa puan, 24ba han bihɛ ba mɛhi gee kiŋɛ, bilam bilam ba ni tamɛ ban ani ni se'em la mɛ. 25Gee sɛba en bihɛ nɔze'ele seko en ka tari gbelegere la, fai nɔze'elego la en ka tari gbelegere la, tara kɔ, dagena kɛleheba sɛba en tameni, gee sɛba en tari tuna, ba wan nyɛ sum ba itegɔ la puan.
26Sɛba han ti'ihɛ ti bamam pu'uheri Yinɛ, gee ka tana ba zɛlehi tara, gee pã'aha ba suya, ba pu'uhegɔ la dela yoo. 27Pu'uhegɔ seko en de fa'a, ka tara galeŋɔ Yinɛ en de Sɔ la nɛŋan en ŋwana. Tu bihera kiibehi, la pokɔpa ba nimbu'ɔ puan, gee ka galena ya mɛhi la timpaberɛ wa zuo yɛla.

english_text:
Warning against Having Favorites
1My friends, if you have faith in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ, you won't treat some people better than others. 2Suppose a rich person wearing fancy clothes and a gold ring comes to one of your meetings. And suppose a poor person dressed in worn-out clothes also comes. 3You must not give the best seat to the one in fancy clothes and tell the one who is poor to stand at the side or sit on the floor. 4This is the same as saying that some people are better than others, and you would be acting like a crooked judge.
5My dear friends, pay attention. God has given a lot of faith to the poor people in this world. God has also promised them a share in his kingdom that he will give to everyone who loves him. 6You mistreat the poor. But isn't it the rich who boss you around and drag you off to court? 7Aren't they the ones who make fun of your Lord?
8 You will do all right, if you obey the most important law in the Scriptures. It is the law that commands us to love others as much as we love ourselves. 9But if you treat some people better than others, you have done wrong, and the Scriptures teach that you have sinned.
10 If you obey every law except one, you are still guilty of breaking them all. 11 The same God who told us to be faithful in marriage also told us not to murder. So even if you are faithful in marriage, but murder someone, you still have broken God's Law.
12Speak and act like people who will be judged by the law that sets us free. 13Do this, because on the day of judgment there will be no pity for those who have not had pity on others. But even in judgment, God is merciful!
Faith and Works
14My friends, what good is it to say you have faith, when you don't do anything to show you really do have faith? Can this kind of faith save you? 15If you know someone who doesn't have any clothes or food, 16you shouldn't just say, “I hope all goes well for you. I hope you will be warm and have plenty to eat.” What good is it to say this, unless you do something to help? 17Faith that doesn't lead us to do good deeds is all alone and dead!
18Suppose someone disagrees and says, “It is possible to have faith without doing kind deeds.”
I would answer, “Prove that you have faith without doing kind deeds, and I will prove that I have faith by doing them.” 19You surely believe there is only one God. That's fine. Even demons believe this, and it makes them shake with fear.
20Does some stupid person want proof that faith without deeds is useless? 21 Well, our ancestor Abraham pleased God by putting his son Isaac on the altar to sacrifice him. 22Now you see how Abraham's faith and deeds worked together. He proved his faith was real by what he did. 23 This is what the Scriptures mean by saying, “Abraham had faith in God, and God accepted him.” That's how Abraham became God's friend.
24You can now see that we please God by what we do and not only by what we believe. 25 For example, Rahab had been a prostitute. But she pleased God when she welcomed the spies and sent them home by another way.
26Anyone who doesn't breathe is dead, and faith that doesn't do anything is just as dead!
translation_text:
Lugehego kã'aŋɔ
1N suurɔ wa, yamam en tari ninkɔɔra se'em wa sirum nam Daana Yezu Kiresta, en de suŋa daana? 2Se'ere en sɔi la, nɛra han wa'am ya lageŋɔ puan na, pire salema bãhi, yɛ fusunɔ, ti naha me en ka yɛ lɔgesunɔ me kɛ̃' na, 3ti ya han bihɛ nyɛ se'em daana en yɛ fusunɔ la, yele en yeti, “N beleni fum mɛ, zi'ire ka'lam,” gee yele naha la yeti, “Zɛ'a ke ha,” bii “Zi'ire tiŋa,” 4ya ka lugehe la ya puan en bala, lebege gakereba en tari putɛ'be'ero? 5Kelehe ya, n sunɔŋerɛ duma. Yinɛ ka looe la naheduma timpaberɛ wa zuo ti ba dɛna buntateba sakerɛ puan, la ba ta sɔna sɔ'ɔlum la ti Yinɛ biŋe nuurɛ bo' sɛba en nɔŋɛ en la? 6Gee yamam ka nane naha. Dagi buntateba la en bala mugehera ya la? Dagi bamam en dati ya kina tugum zi'ihen la? 7Dagi bamam en tuuri yu'sunɛ se'ere en dikɛ sigɛ ya la?
8 Ya wan iŋɛ suŋa, ya han sirum tum na'am nɔze'elego la wuu gulehegɔ la en yele se'em yeti, “Fum nɔŋɛ fum tadaana wuu fum mɛŋa la.” 9Gee yamam han lugeha nɛreba, ya tum la be'em, ti ze'elego la nyɔkɛ ya ti ya tuue mɛ. 10Se'ere en sɔi la, fum se'em woo en dole ze'elego la za'a, gee tuue zi'an kayima, tuue ze'elego la za'a mɛ. 11 Se'ere en sɔi la, se'em daana en yeti, “Da tum kabohi la,” eŋa mɛa en yeti, “Da ku nɛra.” Bala, fum han ka tum kabohi, gee ku nɛra, fum tuue ze'elego la mɛ. 12Bala, tɔgera gee ita wuu sɛba ti ba wan gakɛ la fai bɔŋa ze'elego la. 13Se'ere en sɔi la gakerɛ kan ta tara nimbɔ'zɔrɛ bo' se'em woo en ka tari nimbɔ'zɔrɛ. Nimbɔ'zɔrɛ ta' gakerɛ mɛ.
Sakerɛ en ka tari tuna
14Beni nyuurɔ en boi bini n suurɔ, se'em han yeti a tari la sakerɛ gee ka tari tuna? Fum sakerɛ la wan faaɛ hɔ bahɛ yoi'? 15Fum suuɔ bii taya han ɛɛra beele, ka tara a nuurɛ dia, 16ti ya ayima yele en yeti, “Kina la suma'ahum. Ɔɔrɔ kan kɛ̃ hɔ, ti fum di tigɛ,” gee ka bo' en, en a inganɛ la en boti sɛla la, beni sum en boi bini? 17Bala, sakerɛ ma'a, han ka tara tuna ki mɛ.
18Gee ayima wan yeti, “Fum tari la sakerɛ, ti mam me tara tuuma.” Eii! Yi pa'alɛ mam fum sakerɛ la ti tuuma ka bɔna bini, gee mam me wan dikɛ la n tuuma la pa'alɛ hɔ n sakerɛ. 19Ya nam ti Yinɛ dela ayima. Ya mɔ ya. Kulekpa'bɛ'ɛhi me pun nam la bala, gee gbi'ira. 20Ya boti ba pa'alɛ ya mɛ? Gɔɔŋɔ wa, ti sakerɛ en ka tari tuuma, ki mɛ? 21 Tu sɔyaaba Aberaham yuum ka di buurɔ a tuuma puan, eŋa en yuum kaabɛ a dayua Aziki kaabegɔ bimbine la zuo la? 22Ya nyɛ ti sakerɛ la yuum vɔi mɛ la a tuuma la, ti a tuuma la bahɛ ti sakerɛ la bi'ɛ. 23 Bala ti gulehegɔ la wa'am asira na, gulehegɔ seko en yeti, “Aberaham nam Yinɛ mɛ, ti Yinɛ bo' en tuntɔɔnɛ,” ti ba yi'ira en Yinɛ zɔ. 24Ya nyɛ ti nɛra diti buurɔ Yinɛ nɛŋan la a tuuma puan gee dagi sakerɛ ma'a zuo. 25 Dagi bala mɛa ti Arehabe, pɔge yalema la yuum di buurɔ Yinɛ nɛŋan a tuuma puan, la eŋa en yuum to'e viihereba la gee bahɛ ti ba doohe sadɔɔ kuyima yehe la? 26Wuu iŋa en ka tari sia ki se'em la, bala mɛa ti sakerɛ en ka tari tuuma me ki.

english_text:
The Tongue
1My friends, we should not all try to become teachers. In fact, teachers will be judged more strictly than others. 2 All of us do many wrong things. But if you can control your tongue, you are mature and able to control your whole body.
3By putting a bit into the mouth of a horse, we can turn the horse in different directions. 4It takes strong winds to move a large sailing ship, but the captain uses only a small rudder to make it go in any direction. 5Our tongues are small too, and yet they brag about big things.
It takes only a spark to start a forest fire! 6 The tongue is like a spark. It is an evil power that dirties the rest of the body and sets a person's entire life on fire with flames that come from hell itself. 7All kinds of animals, birds, reptiles, and sea creatures can be tamed and have been tamed. 8But our tongues get out of control. They are restless and evil, and always spreading deadly poison.
9-10 My dear friends, with our tongues we speak both praises and curses. We praise our Lord and Father, and we curse people who were created to be like God, and this isn't right. 11Can clean water and dirty water both flow from the same spring? 12Can a fig tree produce olives or a grapevine produce figs? Does fresh water come from a well full of salt water?
Wisdom from Above
13 Are any of you wise or sensible? Then show it by living right and by being humble and wise in everything you do. 14But if your heart is full of bitter jealousy and selfishness, don't brag or lie to cover up the truth. 15This kind of wisdom doesn't come from above. It is earthly and selfish and comes from the devil himself. 16Whenever people are jealous or selfish, they cause trouble and do all sorts of cruel things. 17But the wisdom that comes from above leads us to be pure, friendly, gentle, sensible, kind, helpful, genuine, and sincere. 18When peacemakers plant seeds of peace, they will harvest justice.
translation_text:
Zɛleŋa tarega
1Dagi ya zo'e zo'e en wan dɛna pa'aleba n suurɔ, se'ere en sɔi la, ya mi' ti tu sɛba en pa'alɛ la, ba wan gakɛ tu la nima nima. 2Se'ere en sɔi la, tu za'a tuure mɛ. Se'em en ka tuure a tugum puan dela tuuntɔɔ, tana a a iŋa za'a tara la gareŋenɛ. 3Tu han lɛ' Yire nɔya la gareŋenɛ ti tu tana ba, tu nyaŋɛ ba iŋa la za'a mɛ, ŋmɛreha ba tumam n boti zi'an. 4Bii bihɛ ya uurenɔ, ban tibegɛ se'em ti kusebego ma'a za'ara ba kina la. Gee la bala za'a, zugɔ pika ti uuren-mɔneba la dikɛ yule uureŋɔ la pulin, tari ku kina bamam en boti se'em. 5Bala mɛa ti zɛleŋa dɛna iŋa la lɔge pika, gee bahɛ ti asaala ŋmɛ'ɛra nyɔ' la yele kãra.
Bihɛ goo en karegɛ se'em, gee ti bugum pãreŋa ni taaɛ kɔ di filam! 6Zɛleŋa dela bugum. Zɛleŋa en boi tu iŋa wa puan la, dela be'em timpaberɛ. Ka ni galum la inganɛ wa za'a, nyaa taaɛ asaala naaŋɔ la za'a di ta ba'ahɛ gee nyaa taaɛ a mɛŋa dita, bugum timpaberɛ la puan. 7Se'ere en sɔi la, goo duhi woo, niihe, bunsɛlenduma, ko'om puan bunvɔɔhi, ta'am nyɛ malehegɔ mɛ, ti asaala en sirum malehɛ ba, 8gee nɛra ka boi ta'am malehɛ a zɛleŋa wa. A dela bumbe'o en ka tuni vɔ'ɔha, pirɛ la yabega. 9Zɛleŋa kaŋa ti tu tara pɛgera Daana la, la Sɔ la, kaŋa mɛa ti tu tara pɔta bahɛ sɛba ti ba naam ba ti ba wuna la Yinɛ. 10Nɔdinɛ mɛa puan ti sum, la ka' be'o zɛ'ɛta na. N suurɔ, la dagi la ana bala. 11Buleniho wan ta'am bula ko'sumɔ la ko'be'ero me yoi? 12N suurɔ wa, Kinkaŋa wan ta'am wam ta'ama? Bii sinsabega wam mu'uro? La kan malum iŋɛ ti ko'om en tari yaarum, bule ko'sumɔ.
Yɛm buyi'
13Ani en tari yɛm, tara bɔkerɛ ya puan? Pa'alɛ bɔ doohe fum vom sumɔ la puan, ti fum tuni fum tuuma la ma'a ma'a la yɛm. 14Gee ya han tara nintɛrega en ba' gaŋɛ, nyika puti'ira ya puan, da dagum ŋmɛ'ɛri ya nyu'ɔ, gee parena yelemɛŋerɛ la nɛŋan. 15Yɛm buna taaba ka ze'ele saazuo na, gee bu dela timpaberɛ wa zuo, ka dɛna sia puan, gee kulekpa'bɛ'ɛhi yɛm. 16Se'ere en sɔi la, zi'an ti nintɛrega la nyika puti'irɛ bɔna, gbiregeri la tuunfi'iha yima yima me wan bɔna. 17Gee yɛm en ze'ele saazuo na, yia bu dela fa'a, tara suma'ahum, ma'ma, tara waŋa suboolum, pirɛ la nimbɔ'zɔrɛ, tara walesuma, ti fum kan nyɛ lugehego, bii birikɔgenɛ bu puan la fii me. 18Ba burɛ la tuntɔɔnɛ biili suma'ahum puan, bo' sɛba en boti suma'ahum la.

english_text:
Friendship with the World
1Why do you fight and argue with each other? Isn't it because you are full of selfish desires that fight to control your body? 2You want something you don't have, and you will do anything to get it. You will even kill! But you still cannot get what you want, and you won't get it by fighting and arguing. You should pray for it. 3Yet even when you do pray, your prayers are not answered, because you pray just for selfish reasons.
4You people aren't faithful to God! Don't you know if you love the world, you are God's enemies? And if you decide to be a friend of the world, you make yourself an enemy of God. 5Do you doubt the Scriptures that say, “God truly cares about the Spirit he has put in us”? 6 In fact, God treats us with even greater kindness, just as the Scriptures say,
“God opposes everyone
who is proud,
but he blesses all who are humble
with undeserved grace.”
7Surrender to God! Resist the devil, and he will run from you. 8Come near to God, and he will come near to you. Clean up your lives, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you people who can't make up your mind. 9Be sad and sorry and weep. Stop laughing and start crying. Be gloomy instead of glad. 10Be humble in the Lord's presence, and he will honor you.
Saying Cruel Things about Others
11My friends, don't say cruel things about others! If you do, or if you condemn others, you are condemning God's Law. And if you condemn the Law, you put yourself above the Law and refuse to obey either it 12or God who gave it. God is our judge, and he can save or destroy us. What right do you have to condemn anyone?
Warning against Bragging
13 You should know better than to say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to the city. We will do business there for a year and make a lot of money!” 14What do you know about tomorrow? How can you be so sure about your life? It is nothing more than mist that appears for only a little while before it disappears. 15You should say, “If the Lord lets us live, we will do these things.” 16Yet you are stupid enough to brag, and it is wrong to be so proud. 17If you don't do what you know is right, you have sinned.
translation_text:
Tiŋa wa zuo zɔtɔ
1Zaba la nɔkpɛ'ɛma sɛ'a en boi ya puan wa, ze'ele la bɛha na? Ba ka ze'ele la ya kunkoma'ahum la en zaberɛ ya puan la? 2Yan boti sɛla gee kan nyɛ la zuo, ti ya kuura.Ya nini en tɛti la sɛla gee kan nyɛ la zuo, ti ya ŋmɛ'ɛra nɔkpɛ'ɛma gee zabera taaba. Ya ka tari, beni zuo, ya ka soke. 3Ya soke ya gee ka to'e, beni zuo, ya ni soke tuue mɛ, ti ya ta'am di ya ma'a nyɛlum. 4Bunyaalehi wa! Ya ka mi' ti ya nyɔgɛ zɔtɔ la timpaberɛ wa, dela ya dɛna dinduma la Yinɛ? Ŋwana zuo, fum se'em woo en boti fum dɛna timpaberɛ wa zuo zɔ, lebege la Yinɛ dima. 5Bii ya ti'ihɛ ti la dela yoo ti gulehegɔ la yeti, “Yinɛ si'ini mɛ la nyuure la a Sia la ti a bahɛ ti ka bɔna la tɔ la? 6 Gee a malum bɔ'ɔra nɛra woo la zu'uhegɔ zo'e zo'e. Ŋwana zuo ti la gulehɛ yeti,
“Yinɛ zagehɛ pa'alɛ n mɛŋa duma mɛ,
gee bɔ'ɔra la sigehe n mɛŋa duma zu'uhegɔ.”
7Sigehe ya mɛhi ŋwana zuo, bo' Yinɛ. Da bo' ya kulekpa'bɛ'a la sore, gee a wan ɛkɛ gee bahɛ ya. 8Vurege ya du' Yinɛ, gee eŋa me wan vurege du' ya. Pee ya nu'uhi, be'em duma wa, gee pee ya suya, puti'ira ayi' ayi' duma wa. 9Fabele ya, si'ini ya, gee kɛla. Bahɛ ya ti ya lɔ'ɔrɔ lebege kuunɔ, ti ya pupeelum dɛna susageŋɔ. 10Sigehe ya mɛhi Daana la nɛŋan, gee a wan zɛkɛ ya.
Taaba gakerɛ
11Da tɔgera ya be'em bɔ'ɔra taaba, n suurɔ wa. Fum se'em woo en tɔgɛ be'em bo' fum tadaana, bii gakɛ fum tadaana, tɔgɛ la be'em bahɛ ze'elego la zuo, gee gakɛ ze'elego la. Gee fum han gakɛ ze'elego la, fum ka tuni ze'elego la tuuma, gee fum dela ku gakera. 12Nɛra ayima ma'a en bo'ori ze'elego la, gee dɛna ku gakera, se'em en wan ta'am faaɛ gee sagum. Bala, fum dela ani ti fum gakɛ fum tadaana?
Nyɔ'ɔ ŋmɛ'a
13 Kelehe ya, yamam sɛba en yeti, “Zina bii beere tu wan kiŋɛ ke la ke ha, ta kɛ̃' bini yuunɛ, lɛɛbera nyɛta ligeri la.” 14Gee ya pun ka mina sɛla ti beere wan tari na. Ya vom dela bem? Se'ere en sɔi la, ya dela mɛgelum en lu yee fii wa, gee mɛlum. 15Gee yan tugum ni wan yele se'em dela, “La han dɛna Daana la putɛ ɛrɛ, tu wan vɔna, gee tum ŋwana la ŋwana.” 16Gee lan de se'em la, ya ŋmɛ'ɛri nyu'ɔ la ya pa'alɛ mɛhi puan. Nyɔ'ɔ ŋmɛ'a kana taaba woo dela be'em. 17Gee se'em woo en mi' sɛla en de ma'a ti a tum, gee koŋe a tum dɛ, tuue mɛ.

english_text:
Warning to the Rich
1You rich people should cry and weep! Terrible things are going to happen to you. 2 Your treasures have already rotted, and moths have eaten your clothes. 3 Your money has rusted, and the rust will be evidence against you, as it burns your body like fire. Yet you keep on storing up wealth in these last days. 4 You refused to pay the people who worked in your fields, and now their unpaid wages are shouting out against you. The Lord All-Powerful has surely heard the cries of the workers who harvested your crops.
5While here on earth, you have thought only of filling your own stomachs and having a good time. But now you are like fat cattle on their way to be butchered. 6 You have condemned and murdered innocent people, who couldn't even fight back.
Be Patient and Kind
7My friends, be patient until the Lord returns. Think of farmers who wait patiently for the autumn and spring rains to make their valuable crops grow. 8Be patient like those farmers and don't give up. The Lord will soon be here! 9Don't grumble about each other or you will be judged, and the judge is right outside the door.
10My friends, follow the example of the prophets who spoke for the Lord. They were patient, even when they had to suffer. 11 In fact, we praise the ones who endured the most. You remember how patient Job was and how the Lord finally helped him. The Lord did this because he is so merciful and kind.
12 My friends, above all else, don't take an oath. You must not swear by heaven or by earth or by anything else. “Yes” or “No” is all you need to say. If you say anything more, you will be condemned.
13If you are having trouble, you should pray. And if you are feeling good, you should sing praises. 14 If you are sick, ask the church leaders to come and pray for you. Ask them to put olive oil on you in the name of the Lord. 15If you have faith when you pray for sick people, they will get well. The Lord will heal them, and if they have sinned, he will forgive them.
16 If you have sinned, you should tell each other what you have done. Then you can pray for one another and be healed. The prayer of an innocent person is powerful, and it can help a lot. 17 Elijah was just as human as we are, and for three and a half years his prayers kept the rain from falling. 18 But when he did pray for rain, it fell from the skies and made the crops grow.
19My friends, if any followers have wandered away from the truth, you should try to lead them back. 20 If you turn sinners from the wrong way, you will save them from death, and many of their sins will be forgiven.
translation_text:
Buntateba en mugehe nɛreba
1Kelehe ya, yamam buntateba wa, kele ya gee si'ina la nimbɔ'seko en ye' ya zuo na la. 2 Ya tarega la pu'ɛ mɛ, ti bunmɔgela mɔgɛ ya fukãra la. 3Ya salema, la salempɛɛla la di la tiŋanziim, ti ba tiŋanziim la wan dɛna aze'nyɛ daana zɛregɛ ya, bu wan di ya iŋa wuu bugum la. Bihɛ ya, yamam tugum lagehɛ la lɔgerɔ biŋe ba'ahegɔ dabeha wa puan? 4 Kelehe ya! Yɔɔrɛ se'ere en de tuntuneba sɛba en tum ya vatɔ tuuma la ti ya fa' biŋe la kaahi baha me na, ti buneba la kaahega me lu pɛntiireba za'a nɛŋa Daana la tuban. 5Ya vɔi timpaberɛ zuo mɛ la tarega la nyɛlum. Ya di mɛ karegɛ gura ya kum daarɛ. 6Ya ni gakɛ mɛ, gee ku tuuntɔɔ daana, se'em en ka zigɛ la ya.
Suure di'ihego namehegɔ puan
7N suurɔ wa, tari ya sugeri gee gura Daana la lɛbega na. Ti'ihɛ ya bihɛ Kaareba en ni tara sugeri se'em gura ba bumbuura suma la ti sigesaa la burega saa ta wa'am na ni. 8Yamam me tara sugeri bala, gee da kɔ'ɛ ya puti'irɛ. Daana la kinɛ na paaɛ mɛ na en bala. 9N suurɔ wa, da gɔgeni ya la taaba, bala ti ba kan gakɛ ya. Bihɛ ya, Gakera la en bala ze'a kuleŋa nuuren wa! 10La han dɛna la namehegɔ la sugeri yɛla, n suurɔ wa, dole ya sɛla ti nɔtɔgeheba sɛba en tɔgɛ Daana la yu'urɛ puan la daa doohe namehɛ seko woo puan tole la. 11 Yelemɛŋerɛ, tu yi'iri sɛba en sakɛ ŋmibega la, la sunduma. Ya wum Yobe ŋmibega la yele, ya me baŋɛ Daana la puti'irɛ yele dinɛ, Daana la en tari giile la nimbɔ'zɔrɛ se'em.
12 Se'ere en gani za'a n suurɔ wa, da pɔti ya saazuo, bii timpaberɛ wa, bii pɔ yele se'ere. Bahɛ ya ti ya “Ɛ̃ɛ” dɛna ɛ̃ɛ, ti ya “Aayi” dɛna aayi', ti ya da lu sageŋɔ puan.
Sakerɛ Daana Pu'uhegɔ
13Sɛba boi ya puan nameha? Ba pu'uhɛ. Sɛba boi ya puan tara pupeelum? Ba yuuna pɛka yuuma. 14 Sɛba boi ya puan bɛ̃'ɛra? Ba yi' lageŋɔ kiinduma ti ba pu'uhɛ bo' ba, gee sɔ' en tuulum sua la kaam Daana la yu'urɛ puan. 15Sakerɛ pu'uhegɔ la wan faaɛ bã'duma la bahɛ, ti Daana la ihege ba, ti ba se'em en tum be'em wan nyɛ sugeri dia. 16Ŋwana zuo, puti ya ya be'em bɔ'ɔra taaba, gee pu'uha bɔ'ɔra taaba bala ti ya wan nyɛ ya tibegɔ. Tuntɔɔ daana pu'uhegɔ tari la paŋa, gee tuna. 17 Elia yuum dela asaala wuu tumam la, gee yuum pu'uhɛ la ninmu'urɛ ti saa da ni, ti la dikɛ yuuma atã la ŋmarehi siyoobe ti saa sirum ka tɔkɛ timpaberɛ wa zuo. 18 Ti a le pu'uhɛ, ti saazuo ha bo' saa na, ti timpaberɛ wa zuo maalɛ dia. 19N suurɔ, se'em han bɔna ya puan bɔregɛ yelemɛŋerɛ wa puan, ti se'em tari en lebena, 20 ya mina ti, se'em woo en tari be'em daana a tuure puan lebe na la, wan faaɛ be'em daana la sia kum puan bahɛ, gee ti Yinɛ pi' be'em daana la be'em zo'e zo'e.

english_text:
1From Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ.
To God's people who are scattered like foreigners in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.
2God the Father decided to choose you as his people, and his Spirit has made you holy. You have obeyed Jesus Christ and are sprinkled with his blood.
I pray that God will be kind to you and will keep on giving you peace!
A Real Reason for Hope
3Praise God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. God is so good, and by raising Jesus from death, he has given us new life and a hope that lives on. 4 God has something stored up for you in heaven, where it will never decay or be ruined or disappear.
5You have faith in God, whose power will protect you until the last day. Then he will save you, just as he has always planned to do. 6On that day you will be glad, even if you have to go through many hard trials for a while. 7 Your faith will be like gold that has been tested in a fire. And these trials will prove that your faith is worth much more than gold that can be destroyed. They will show that you will be given praise and honor and glory when Jesus Christ returns.
8You have never seen Jesus, and you don't see him now. But still you love him and have faith in him, and no words can tell how glad and happy 9you are to be saved. This is why you have faith.
10Some prophets told how God would treat you with undeserved grace, and they searched hard to find out more about the way you would be saved. 11The Spirit of Christ was in them and was telling them how Christ would suffer and would then be given great honor. So they searched to find out exactly who Christ would be and when this would happen. 12But they were told that they were serving you and not themselves. They preached to you by the power of the Holy Spirit, who was sent from heaven. And their message was only for you, even though angels would like to know more about it.
Chosen To Live a Holy Life
13Be alert and think straight. Put all your hope in how God will treat you with undeserved grace when Jesus Christ appears. 14Behave like obedient children. Don't let your lives be controlled by your desires, as they used to be. 15Always live as God's holy people should, because God is the one who chose you, and he is holy. 16 That's why the Scriptures say, “I am the holy God, and you must be holy too.”
17You say that God is your Father, but God doesn't have favorites! He judges all people by what they do. So you must honor God while you live as strangers here on earth. 18You were rescued from the useless way of life you learned from your ancestors. But you know you were not rescued by such things as silver or gold that don't last forever. 19 You were rescued by the precious blood of Christ, that spotless and innocent lamb. 20Christ was chosen even before the world was created, but because of you, he did not come until these last days. 21And when he did come, it was to lead you to have faith in God, who raised him from death and honored him in a glorious way. This is why you have put your faith and hope in God.
22You obeyed the truth, and your souls were made pure. Now you sincerely love each other. But you must keep on loving with all your heart. 23Do this because God has given you new birth by his message that lives on forever. 24 The Scriptures say,
“Humans wither like grass,
and their glory fades
like wild flowers.
Grass dries up,
and flowers fall
to the ground.
25But what the Lord has said
will stand forever.”
Our good news to you is what the Lord has said.
translation_text:
Pu'uhegɔ
1Mam Pita en de Yezu Kiresta tuntuna, en gulehɛ gɔŋɔ wa bɔ'ɔra sɛba en nɔgɛ bɔna zi'an woo, Pɔntusi, Galatia, Kapadosia, Esiya, la Bitiniya tihi puan la. 2Sɛba ti Yinɛ en de Sɔ la daa pun te'ele looe ba, maahum ba, gee duuhe ba la a Fa'a Sia la, ti ba nana Yezu Kiresta, gee ti a miihi ba la Yezu ziim la.
Zu'uhegɔ la suma'ahum zo'e zo'e dɛna ya dinɛ.
Beere putɛ'vua
3Sum dɛna Yinɛ en de tu Daana Yezu Kiresta Sɔ la dinɛ! A nimbɔ'zɔrɛ kãtɛ la zuo, a bo' tu la dɔgum paalemɔ ti tu tara beere putɛ'vua doohe Yezu Kiresta vo'ore a kum la puan. 4A yi ya mɛ ti ya to'e lɔgerɔ seto en ka sageni, ka galum, ka kuregera, en maahum biŋe saazuo ha gura ya. 5Yamam sɛba ti Yinɛ paŋa gu'ura ya doohe ya sakerɛ puan la, ya faarɛ la wan niiɛ ba'ahegɔ saŋa la na. 6Dina puan ti ya nyɛɛna, la han pun dɛna ti nananawa, saŋa fii wa, ya namehɛ kãra yima yima doohe mageha yima yamam puan 7ti ya yelemɛŋerɛ sakerɛ la en tari tibehum gana salema, sakerɛ wa en tari tibehum gana salema wa, en pun tana Sagena la, gee ba wan kelum magehɛ bu la bugum bihɛ, bala mɛa ti ba wan magehɛ ya sakerɛ la bihɛ, gee de wan tara pɛka la suŋa, la na'ahegɔ, Yezu Kiresta han ta niiɛ na. 8La yan pun ka nyɛ en la, ya nɔŋɛ en mɛ. La yan pun ka nyɛ en nananawa la, ya nam en mɛ, gee nyɛɛna mɛ la nyɛɛma kãtɛ sɛ'a en ka tari tɛka pirɛ suŋa. 9Se'ere en sɔi la, ya to'ore la ya sakerɛ yɔɔrɛ en de ya sɛɛhi faarɛ la. 10Han dɛna faarɛ dina wa yele, nɔtɔgeheba sɛba en yuum purɛ zu'uhegɔ la en wan dɛna ya dinɛ la, ma'ɛ ba mɛhi mɛ, viihɛ, gee ɛ bu paaɛ paaɛ, 11viihera ɛɛra nɛresɛka, la sansɛka ti Kiresta Sia la en boi ba puan la ta pa'alɛ ba, doohe la Sia la en te'ele yele ba namehegɔ seko taaba en maahum gura Kiresta, la na'ahegɔ seko en dole ku poore. 12La yuum niiɛ pa'alɛ ba yeti, ba ka tuni bɔ'ɔra la ba mɛhi, gee tumam, doohe yelesɛ'a en nyaa muulɛ bo' ya nananawa, doohe sɛba en tari faarɛ yelehum wa na bo' ya la, doohe Fa'a Sia la ti Yinɛ tum en saazuo ha bahɛ na la.Yele sɛ'a ti suŋereba mu'ɛ nini ti ba nyɛ la.
Fa'a vom yi'a
13Ŋwana zuo, maahum ya puti'ira ti ya tum. Tana ya mɛhi tara. Bahɛ ya ti ya puti'ira za'a bɔna zu'uhegɔ seko ti Yezu Kiresta wan tari na bo' ya, a han ta niiɛ na la puan. 14Wuu yan de kɔma en nane la, da naaɛ ya la kunkoma'ahum sebo taaba ti ya yuum pun tara, yan yuum nan ka mi' la. 15Gee wuu se'em en yi' ya la, en de fa'a se'em la, deni ya Yinɛ tuulum nɛreba ya mɛhi, ya itegɔ woo puan. 16 La gulehɛ yeti, “Deni ya Yinɛ tuulum nɛreba, se'ere en sɔi la mam dela Fa'a.”
17Yamam han yi'ira en Sɔ, se'em en gakeri nɛra woo ka tara ninkɔɔra, gee nɛra woo la a tuuma en de se'em la, voni ya la dabeem ya nɔka saŋa wa puan. 18Ya mi ti Yinɛ yɔ mɛ to'e ya yehe vom yoo sebo ti ya to'e ya yaabeduma zi'an la. A ka yɔ mɛ la lɔgeseto en sageni, ana wuu salempɛɛla bii salema, 19gee Kiresta tuulum ziim en ani wuu kaabegɔ pebila en ka bɛ̃' bii tara dɛkɔ se'em la. 20Yinɛ yuum pun maahum en mɛ gee ti timpaberɛ wa baŋɛ pi'ilum, gee ta niiɛ en ba'ahegɔ saŋa wa puan, yamam zuo. 21Doohe eŋa puan ti ya wa'am na nam Yinɛ, se'em en ihege en a kum puan la, gee bo' en na'ahegɔ, ti ya sakerɛ, la ya beere puti'irɛ la bɔna Yinɛ zi'an.
22Nananawa ti ya pee ya sɛɛhi doohe yan nam yelemɛŋerɛ la, nyaa tara yelemɛŋerɛ nɔŋerɛ la, nɔŋɛ ya taaba paaɛ paaɛ ya suya puan ha. 23Ba dɔgɛ ya la dɔgum paalum, dagena la biiliho sebo en pu'uri, gee biiliho sebo en ka pu'uri, ba malum dɔgɛ ya doohe la Yinɛ yelehum vua la en ka malum ba'aha la puan. 24 Se'ere en sɔi la,
“Asaala woo ani mɛ wuu muɔ la
ti ba suŋa za'a ana wuu mɔpuuro la.
Muɔ ku'uri mɛ,
ti mɔpuuro zɔgera,
25gee Daana yelehum la kɔ'ɔm bɔna mɛ wuuha wuuha.”
Yelehum buna wa dela faarɛ yelehum sebo ti ba muulɛ bo' ya la.

english_text:
A Living Stone and a Holy Nation
1Stop being hateful! Quit trying to fool people, and start being sincere. Don't be jealous or say cruel things about others. 2Be like newborn babies who are thirsty for the pure spiritual milk that will help you grow and be saved. 3 You have already found out how good the Lord really is.
4Come to Jesus Christ. He is the living stone people have rejected, but which God has chosen and highly honored. 5And now you are living stones being used to build a spiritual house. You are also a group of holy priests, and with the help of Jesus Christ you will offer sacrifices that please God. 6 It is just as God says in the Scriptures,
“Look! I am placing in Zion
a choice and precious
cornerstone.
No one who has faith
in this one
will be disappointed.”
7 You are followers of the Lord, and this stone is precious to you. But it isn't precious to those who refuse to follow him. They are the builders who tossed aside the stone that turned out to be the most important one of all. 8 They disobeyed the message and stumbled and fell over this stone, because they were doomed.
9 But you are God's chosen and special people. You are a group of royal priests and a holy nation. God has brought you out of darkness into his marvelous light. Now you must tell all the wonderful things he has done. The Scriptures say,
10 “Once you were nobody.
Now you are God's people.
At one time no one
had mercy on you.
Now God has treated you
with kindness.”
Live as God's Servants Should
11Dear friends, you are foreigners and strangers on this earth. So I beg you not to surrender to those desires that fight against you. 12Always let others see you behaving properly, even though they may still accuse you of doing wrong. Then on the day of judgment, they will honor God by telling the good things they saw you do.
13The Lord wants you to obey all human authorities, especially the Emperor, who rules over everyone. 14You must also obey governors, because they are sent by the Emperor to punish criminals and to praise good citizens. 15God wants you to silence stupid and ignorant people by doing right. 16You are free, but still you are God's servants, and you must not use your freedom as an excuse for doing wrong. 17Respect everyone and show special love for God's people. Honor God and respect the Emperor.
The Example of Christ's Suffering
18Servants, you must obey your masters and always show respect to them. Do this, not only to those who are kind and thoughtful, but also to those who are cruel. 19God will bless you, even if others treat you unfairly for being loyal to him. 20You don't gain anything by being punished for some wrong you have done. But God will bless you, if you have to suffer for doing something good. 21After all, God chose you to suffer as you follow in the footsteps of Christ, who set an example by suffering for you.
22 Christ did not sin
or ever tell a lie.
23 Although he was abused,
he never tried to get even.
And when he suffered,
he made no threats.
Instead, he had faith in God,
who judges fairly.
24 Christ carried the burden
of our sins.
He was nailed to the cross,
so we would stop sinning
and start living right.
By his cuts and bruises
you are healed.
25You had wandered away
like sheep.
Now you have returned
to the one
who is your shepherd
and protector.
translation_text:
Ɛ̃berɛ, la Yinɛ en looe nɛre sɛba
1Bala, yehe ya mɛhi, yele ana wa puan. Putoo, wikerɛ, birekɔgenɛ, nintɛrega, la yu'sageŋɔ. 2Wuu yan de bilɛɛhi la, kɔ'ɔm leebere ya mɛ la Sia puan bi'ihum sumɔ la, bala ti bu wan bahɛ ti ya zɔ'ɔra ya faarɛ la puan, 3 ya han sirum lem mɛ nyɛ Daana la en ani suŋa se'em.
4Wa'am ya a zi'an na, eŋa en de vom ɛ̃berɛ kugere la, la saaleba en pun zagehɛ en la, gee eŋa ti Yinɛ looe, ti a dɛna tuulum lɔkɔ Yinɛ nɛŋan. 5Wuu yan de vom kuga en dikɛ ya mɛhi mɛ Sia yire, deni ya tuulum malema duma, kaabera sia puan kaabegɔ en tigɛ Yinɛ nini doohe Yezu Kiresta puan. 6 Se'ere en sɔi la, la boi gulehegɔ la puan yeti,
“Bihɛ, n biŋere la ɛ̃berɛ kugere Zaayɔn,
ɛ̃berɛ kugere se'ere ti ba looe, gee ti de dɛna tuulum kugere.
Se'em woo en nam en, vi kan di en.”
7 Ti fum se'em woo en nam, a dela tuulum lɔkɔ bo' fum, gee sɛba en ka nam la,
“Ɛ̃berɛ kuge se'ere ti mɛteba zagehɛ la,
dinɛ en de kuge sunɛ, tara ɛ̃berɛ la,”
8 gee
“Me dɛna kuge se'ere ti ba sɛrena de zuo luta,
dɛna tansɛka en piti ba lɔbera.”
Ban piti luta la dela, ban ka nam yelehum la, wuu ban pun maahum ba ti ba iŋɛ se'em la. 9 Gee yamam dela buuri se'ere ti Yinɛ looe, ya dela malemaduma nabiihi, dɛna tuulum timpaberɛ, Yinɛ mɛŋa nɛreba, ti ya muulɛ tuunkãra sɛ'a en de se'em daana en yi' ya lika puan yehe niihum kãtɛ puan na la dinɛ.
10 Ya daa nan ka de a nɛreba,
gee nananawa, ya dela Yinɛ nɛreba.
Ya daa nan ka to'e nimbɔ'zɔrɛ,
gee nananawa, ya to'e nimbɔ'zɔrɛ.
Vɔni ya wuu Yinɛ yamehi
11N sunɔŋerɛ duma mam ka'ani ya mɛ la ninmu'urɛ, wuu yan de saama, la nɔgereba la, ti ya yehe ya mɛhi ingɔŋɔ wa kɔrehi sɛ'a en zaberɛ la ya sia la puan. 12Tara ya mɛhi suŋa sɛba en dagi Yuuduma la zi'an, bala ti ban pun dikɛ ya yi' be'em duma la, ba wan nyɛ ya tunsuma la, gee pɛgera Yinɛ, a han ta wa'am na ti a gakɛ.
13Daana la zuo, nane ya asaala tigere woo kpe'eŋo, yele yele wuu Timbihega nɛŋa daana se'em en sɔi ya za'a bihera la, 14bii timbihega duma ti a tum ba, ti ba namehɛ tuunfi'iha duma, gee pɛgera sɛba en tuni ma'a la. 15Se'ere en sɔi la, la dela Yinɛ sumboolum ti ya han ita sɛla en de ma'a, ya wan ma'ɛ gɔɔnɔ la en ka mi' la nɔya. 16Yamam en de Yinɛ yamehi la, vɔni ya fai, gee la bala za'a, da dikɛ ya fai bɔŋa la tuna be'em. 17Na'ahɛ ya nɛra woo. Nɔŋɛ ya suurɔ seto en de sakereba la. Zoti ya Yinɛ. Na'aheri ya timbihega nɛŋa daana la.
Kiresta namehegɔ makerɛ
18Yamehi, nane ya ya kpɛ'ɛnduma kpe'eŋo woo la na'ahegɔ, dagi la sɛba en iti ya suŋa, gee ana ma'ma la ya la ma'a, gee sɛba me en vɛgeleni ya. 19Se'ere en sɔi la, la dela yɔɔrɛ bɔ'ɔra ya, yan mi' Yinɛ la, ya han ŋmibera too, gee nyɛta namehegɔ seko en dagi tuuntɔɔ. 20Ya han ŋmibera ban ŋmɛ'ɛri ya sɛla ti ya tuue puan, beni nyuurɔ en boi bini? Gee ya han ŋmibera yan tum ma'a gee ti ba namehɛ ya de zuo, Yinɛ nini tigɛ mɛ la ya. 21Ŋwana zuo ti Yinɛ yi' ya la, beni zuo, Kiresta namehɛ mɛ bo' yamam ti ya biha bala niira a nama la.
22 “A ka tari be'em,
pã'ahegɔ ka tabelɛ ze'ele a nuuren na.”
23Ban wa tu' en la, a ka leregere la tuurɛ. Ban wa nameha en la, a ka lebehe ba. Gee a dikɛ a mɛŋa bo' la se'em en gakeri tuuntɔɔ la. 24 Eŋa mɛŋa en zi' tu be'em a iŋa puan pumpuuredɔɔ la zuo. Be'em la en ki tumam puan la, tu nyaa wan vɔna tuuntɔɔ vom. A pɔgeleŋɔ la puan, ti ya nyɛ tibegɔ. 25 Se'ere en sɔi la, ya daa bɔregɛ mɛ wuu piihi la, gee nananawa, ya ŋmɛregɛ lebe la dunkiina sɛka en guri ya sɛɛhi la zi'an na.

english_text:
Wives and Husbands
1 If you are a wife, you must put your husband first. Even if he opposes our message, you will win him over by what you do. No one else will have to say anything to him, 2because he will see how you honor God and live a pure life. 3 Don't depend on things like fancy hairdos or gold jewelry or expensive clothes to make you look beautiful. 4Be beautiful in your heart by being gentle and quiet. This kind of beauty will last, and God considers it very special.
5Long ago those women who worshiped God and put their hope in him made themselves beautiful by putting their husbands first. 6For example, Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him her master. You are her true children, if you do right and don't let anything frighten you.
7 If you are a husband, you should be thoughtful of your wife. Treat her with honor, because she isn't as strong as you are, and she shares with you in the gift of life. Then nothing will stand in the way of your prayers.
Suffering for Doing Right
8Finally, all of you should agree and have concern and love for each other. You should also be kind and humble. 9Don't be hateful and insult people just because they are hateful and insult you. Instead, treat everyone with kindness. You are God's chosen ones, and he will bless you. The Scriptures say,
10 “Do you really love life?
Do you want to be happy?
Then stop saying cruel things
and quit telling lies.
11Give up your evil ways
and do right,
as you find and follow
the road to peace.
12The Lord watches over
everyone who obeys him,
and he listens
to their prayers.
But he opposes everyone
who does evil.”
13Can anyone really harm you for being eager to do good deeds? 14 Even if you have to suffer for doing good things, God will bless you. So stop being afraid and don't worry about what people might do. 15Honor Christ and let him be the Lord of your life.
Always be ready to give an answer when someone asks you about your hope. 16Give a kind and respectful answer and keep your conscience clear. This way you will make people ashamed for saying bad things about your good conduct as a follower of Christ. 17You are better off to obey God and suffer for doing right than to suffer for doing wrong.
18Christ died once for our sins.
An innocent person died
for those who are guilty.
Christ did this
to bring you to God,
when his body
was put to death
and his spirit
was made alive.
19Christ then preached to the spirits that were being kept in prison. 20 They had disobeyed God while Noah was building the boat, but God had been patient with them. Eight people went into that boat and were brought safely through the flood.
21Those flood waters were like baptism that now saves you. But baptism is more than just washing your body. It means turning to God with a clear conscience, because Jesus Christ was raised from death. 22Christ is now in heaven, where he sits at the right side of God. All angels, authorities, and powers are under his control.
translation_text:
Pɔgeba la Sireba
1 Pɔgeba, bala mɛa, sigehe ya mɛhi bo' ya mɛhi sireba, ti basɛba han pun ka nam yelehum la, ba wan nyaŋɛ ba, gee pun ka yele se'ere, gee ba pɔgeba aŋa la ma'a, 2ba han nyɛta ya zulaam vom la, la ya na'ahegɔ seko en boi ya vom puan la. 3 Da yeen nɔni ya ya mɛhi yiŋa, doohe ya zuto gulega, la salema lɔgerɔ yɛa, bii futo da'a en kpe'em, 4gee tugum bahɛ ya ti ya nunɔm la bɔna ya puan, ya ana ma'ma, gee tara bããlam sia vom la en de sunsɛka en ka tari ba'ahegɔ, tara tuulum kãtɛ Yinɛ nɛŋan la. 5Sadɔɔ kuna ti diimen diimen tuulum pɔgeba la en yuum tari beere puti'irɛ Yinɛ puan la, yuum nɔna. Nana ba sireba en tari kpe'eŋo seko woo la. 6 Bala ti Saara nam Aberaham, pun ta yi'ira en a daana.Ya me dela a poyɔɔhi, wuu ya han ita sɛla en ani suŋa, gee ka bahɛ ti dabeem sãɛ ya.
7 Sireba, bala mɛa, me zu'uhi ya ya pɔgeba, yan boi la taaba la, na'ahera fum pɔga, la eŋa en pun dɛna tɔregɔ lɔkɔ la, se'ere en sɔi la, ba wan ta to'e Yinɛ vom bo'olum la mɛ. Iti ya bala ti sɛla da gu'ura ya pu'uhegɔ.
Itesuŋɔ namehegɔ
8Ba'ahegɔ, ya woo tara Sia la nɔyinɛ vom la, zɔta taaba nimbu'ɔ, nɔŋɛ ya taaba, tari ya taaba giile, gee sigehe ya mɛhi ya suya puan bo' taaba. 9Da dikɛ be'em yɔ be'em, bii kɛhega yɔ kɛhega. Gee lan de se'em dela, lɛbehera sum. Ŋwana zuo ti Yinɛ yi' ya, ti ya wa'am na to'e sum la. 10 Se'ere en sɔi la,
“Sɛba en boti vom,
gee bɔta ti ba nyɛ dabeha suma la,
ba ta'na ba zɛlehi da tɔgera be'em,
ba da tara ba nɔya pã'aha.
11Ba bire ba pɔya bahɛ be'em, gee ita suŋa.
Ba ɛɛra suma'ahum, gee mu'ɛ nini dɔla bɔ.
12Se'ere en sɔi la, Daana la nini gã' la tuuntɔɔ duma zuo,
ti a tuba ana kɛli la ba pu'uhegɔ.
Gee Daana la nɛŋa ka loregere la sɛba en tuni be'em.”
13Nananawa, ani n wan daam ya, ya han mu'ɛ nini ti ya ita sɛla en ani suŋa? 14 Gee ya han pun nameha yan iti sɛla en de ma'a zuo, sum boi mɛ la ya. Da zoti ya ba, gee me da bahɛ ti la daana ya, 15gee ya suya puan, tugum malum gurɛ ya Kiresta ti a dɛna daana. Saŋa woo, maahum ya ti ya tɔgɛ po'e ya mɛhi, se'em en soke ya ti ya pa'alɛ en ya beere puti'irɛ wa, lerege ya en bããlam la Yinɛ zoolum. 16Tari ya susunɛ, ti ba han pun yi'ira ya yu'yooro, sɛba en keheri ya itesuŋɔ Kiresta puan la, vi wan di ba. 17Se'ere en sɔi la, la ani suŋa ti fum nyɛ namehegɔ fum itesuŋɔ zuo, namehegɔ la han dɛna Yinɛ sumboolum, nyana fum nyɛ namehegɔ be'em tuuma zuo. 18Kiresta me wa namehɛ mɛ buyina, tumam za'a be'em zuo.
